details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cna.title: Enforce maximum recursion depth in encoding/asn1

descriptions.value: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.

cna.title: Quadratic complexity in WordDecoder.DecodeHeader in mime

descriptions.value: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.

notes.text:
An update for kernel is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The kernel packages contain the Linux kernel, the core of any Linux operating system.

Security Fix(es):

* kernel: tcp: restrict SO_ATTACH_FILTER to priv users (CVE-2026-53236)

* kernel: fuse: re-lock request before replacing page cache folio (CVE-2026-53388)

* kernel: net: shaper: rework the VALID marking (again) (CVE-2026-64027)

* kernel: net/handshake: hand off the pinned file reference to accept_doit (CVE-2026-63979)

* kernel: net/handshake: Drain pending requests at net namespace exit (CVE-2026-63978)

* kernel: af_unix: Fix UAF read of tail->len in unix_stream_data_wait() (CVE-2026-64109)

* kernel: net/handshake: Take a long-lived file reference at submit (CVE-2026-64523)

* kernel: net: gro: fix double aggregation of flush-marked skbs (CVE-2026-68136)

* kernel: net/packet: avoid fanout hook re-registration after unregister (CVE-2026-68338)

* kernel: scsi: target: core: Fix iSCSI ISID use-after-free in REGISTER AND MOVE (CVE-2026-72083)

* kernel: KVM: s390: pci: Reject adapter interrupt forwarding if already enabled (CVE-2026-74515)

* kernel: net: smc: fix splice entry lifetime imbalance in smc_rx_splice (CVE-2026-74631)

* kernel: usb: usbfs: fix use-after-free of usb_device in usbdev_release() (CVE-2026-80824)

* kernel: smb: client: clear setuid/setgid bit on write with cifsacl/modefromsid/posix extensions (CVE-2026-89638)

* kernel: vfio/pci: clear vdev->msi_perm after freeing it on init failure (CVE-2026-89777)

* kernel: md/raid5-ppl: fix use-after-free in ppl_do_flush() (CVE-2026-93262)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* x86/microcode: Add platform mask to Intel microcode "old" list [RHEL-10] [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-212778)

* net: NULL pointer deref kernel panic in fib6_walk_continue under heavy VRF churn [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-245489)

* backport fixes for lockdep issues reported with rt-debug [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-259937)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) component. The `fuse_try_move_folio()` function, responsible for managing page cache folios, fails to re-lock a request after initially unlocking it on a successful path. This oversight allows another function, `fuse_chan_abort()`, to prematurely free critical input/output arguments (`fuse_io_args`). Consequently, subsequent operations attempting to access these freed arguments can lead to a use-after-free vulnerability, potentially allowing an attacker to cause a system crash or execute arbitrary code.

notes.text: kernel: fuse: re-lock request before replacing page cache folio
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires local access and relies on winning a race condition during concurrent abort operations on user-space filesystem requests. An unprivileged local user must have permissions to interact with or mount a FUSE filesystem to initiate the conflicting input/output transactions. Successful exploitation could destabilize kernel memory, resulting in a system crash or potential privilege escalation.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's af_unix (UNIX domain sockets) component. A race condition in the unix_stream_data_wait() function allows a local attacker to trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability. This occurs because the function peeks at a socket buffer without proper locking, enabling another thread to free the buffer while it is still being referenced. Successful exploitation of this UAF could lead to system instability or potentially information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: af_unix: Fix UAF read of tail->len in unix_stream_data_wait()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Use-after-free read in the AF_UNIX stream receive path can occur because unix_stream_data_wait reads the length of the tail SKB after observing the receive queue without a lock that protects against dequeue and free. A local process can trigger the race by using AF_UNIX stream sockets with peeking and normal receive operations on the same socket so that one thread waits on stale queue state while another thread removes and frees the SKB. For the CVSS the PR:L because attacker controlled local code is needed to create the socket state and race the recv operations, but no administrative privilege is required. The issue is not network reachable because AF_UNIX sockets are local IPC. Impact is at least local denial of service via kernel warning or crash, and in the paranoid score limited confidentiality or integrity impact is kept possible because this is a real UAF read of a freed kernel object, not just a pure logic hang.

To mitigate this flaw on hosts that do not operate as storage target servers, prevent the LIO target kernel modules from loading:

1. Create a configuration file to prevent loading the target modules:
# echo "install iscsi_target_mod /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/disable-iscsi_target.conf
# echo "install target_core_mod /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/disable-target_core.conf

2. Stop the SCSI target daemon if active:
# systemctl stop target.service

Warning: Modifying kernel module loading or stopping target.service requires a service restart or system reboot, and will immediately interrupt active storage connections on systems acting as storage targets.

If the machine must function as an iSCSI target, use network firewall rules to restrict access to the iSCSI target port (TCP port 3260) strictly to authorized initiator hosts.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `smc_rx_splice` function within the net: smc component. This vulnerability arises from an imbalance in the lifetime management of splice entries, where page references are not properly handled before being passed to `splice_to_pipe()`. This can lead to a reference count underflow, resulting in a use-after-free condition. A successful exploitation of this flaw could potentially lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net: smc: fix splice entry lifetime imbalance in smc_rx_splice
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free can occur in the SMC splice receive path because smc_rx_splice() passed pages to splice_to_pipe() before taking the page and socket references that cover each splice entry lifetime. If splice_to_pipe() drops entries that were not queued, smc_rx_spd_release() can release state before matching references exist, while queued entries are released later through pipe buffer callbacks. This can underflow page refcounts and leave stale page lifetime state, creating a kernel memory safety issue rather than a simple crash-only bug. For the CVSS the PR:L is used because a local process is typically required to create or use an SMC socket and call splice(), even if no administrative privileges are required. Impact is at least local denial of service via kernel crash and in worst case may allow confidentiality or integrity impact due to use-after-free memory corruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's USB subsystem (usbfs). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb node could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability. This occurs because the usb_device structure is prematurely freed before all pending operations are completed. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a system crash or potentially privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: usb: usbfs: fix use-after-free of usb_device in usbdev_release()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel usbfs (USB user-space) subsystem, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other Red Hat products that ship the Red Hat kernel. In usbdev_release(), the reference to the struct usb_device is dropped before the list of completed asynchronous URBs is drained, and the drain path (free_async() calling dec_usb_memory_use_count()) then reads back through the already-freed device, for example via bus_to_hcd(ps->dev->bus). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb device node could mmap() the file descriptor, submit an asynchronous URB whose buffer lies inside that mapping, wait for the device to be unplugged so that the usbfs reference becomes the last reference and the device is freed, and then unmap and close the file descriptor, deterministically triggering the use-after-free. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a kernel crash (denial of service) or potentially privilege escalation. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): although triggering the use-after-free itself is deterministic and not a race, reliably converting it into privilege escalation requires high attack complexity. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat products.

2. Persist this setting by ensuring `nosuid` is present in the mount options within `/etc/fstab`:
```
//server/share /mnt/cifs cifs credentials=/etc/samba/creds,nosuid 0 0
```

3. Alternatively, if CIFS mounts are not required on the system, disable autoloading of the kernel module:
```
echo "install cifs /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/cifs.conf
```

Caveats:
Enforcing `nosuid` prevents any executable located on the mount point from running with elevated setuid or setgid privileges. Blacklisting the `cifs` module prevents all SMB/CIFS network file systems from mounting. Remounting filesystems can disrupt ongoing read and write operations.

cwe.name: Expired Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's vfio/pci component. During device initialization, a memory pointer is not properly cleared after being freed, leading to a use-after-free and double-free vulnerability. A local attacker could exploit this flaw to cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: vfio/pci: clear vdev->msi_perm after freeing it on init failure
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free and double-free flaw in the Linux kernel's vfio/pci subsystem has been rated Important by Red Hat. When initialization of the per-device MSI permission table fails (for example, when an underlying allocation fails with -ENOMEM), the error path in vfio_msi_cap_len() frees vdev->msi_perm but leaves the dangling pointer stored in the per-device vfio_pci_core_device structure, which persists across open/close cycles. A local attacker with access to a VFIO PCI device could trigger this failed initialization path and then, on a subsequent open or close of the device, cause the freed object to be reused for MSI config-space accesses (dereferencing and calling the freed perm->readfn/perm->writefn function pointers) or to be freed a second time in vfio_config_free(). This can lead to a kernel panic and system crash (denial of service) or potentially to execution of arbitrary code with elevated privileges. Red Hat rates this flaw as Important with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H); the higher CVE.org score of 8.8 reflects a lower attack-complexity assessment, whereas Red Hat considers exploitation to depend on reliably steering a memory-allocation failure during device initialization. Within Red Hat's affected product scope, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 and 7 (kernel and kernel-rt ELS streams) are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present, while the vulnerable code is present in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 (kernel and kernel-rt), Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and Red Hat OpenShift versions that ship an affected kernel, and fixes are being pursued through the responsible engineering teams.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potentially escalate privileges through a use-after-free vulnerability in the RAID-5 Partial Parity Log (PPL) component. During flush operations, the system improperly continues to access an input/output (I/O) tracking structure after it has already been released. This memory corruption can destabilize the operating system and cause the kernel to crash.

Prevent the `raid456` kernel module from loading if software RAID 4, 5, or 6 functionality is not required.

1. Add the blacklist configuration by creating `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-raid456.conf` with the following entries:
blacklist raid456
install raid456 /bin/true

2. Unload the module if it is currently loaded:
# modprobe -r raid456

Warning: If software RAID 4, 5, or 6 is currently in use or required for storage arrays, this workaround cannot be applied, as disabling the module will prevent storage devices from functioning. A system reboot may be required if the module is actively in use by existing mounts.

notes.text:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udp: Deal with race between UDP socket address change and rehash

If a UDP socket changes its local address while it's receiving
datagrams, as a result of connect(), there is a period during which
a lookup operation might fail to find it, after the address is changed
but before the secondary hash (port and address) and the four-tuple
hash (local and remote ports and addresses) are updated.

Secondary hash chains were introduced by commit 30fff9231fad ("udp:
bind() optimisation") and, as a result, a rehash operation became
needed to make a bound socket reachable again after a connect().

This operation was introduced by commit 719f835853a9 ("udp: add
rehash on connect()") which isn't however a complete fix: the
socket will be found once the rehashing completes, but not while
it's pending.

This is noticeable with a socat(1) server in UDP4-LISTEN mode, and a
client sending datagrams to it. After the server receives the first
datagram (cf. _xioopen_ipdgram_listen()), it issues a connect() to
the address of the sender, in order to set up a directed flow.

Now, if the client, running on a different CPU thread, happens to
send a (subsequent) datagram while the server's socket changes its
address, but is not rehashed yet, this will result in a failed
lookup and a port unreachable error delivered to the client, as
apparent from the following reproducer:

  LEN=$(($(cat /proc/sys/net/core/wmem_default) / 4))
  dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1 count=${LEN} of=tmp.in

  while :; do
  	taskset -c 1 socat UDP4-LISTEN:1337,null-eof OPEN:tmp.out,create,trunc &
  	sleep 0.1 || sleep 1
  	taskset -c 2 socat OPEN:tmp.in UDP4:localhost:1337,shut-null
  	wait
  done

where the client will eventually get ECONNREFUSED on a write()
(typically the second or third one of a given iteration):

  2024/11/13 21:28:23 socat[46901] E write(6, 0x556db2e3c000, 8192): Connection refused

This issue was first observed as a seldom failure in Podman's tests
checking UDP functionality while using pasta(1) to connect the
container's network namespace, which leads us to a reproducer with
the lookup error resulting in an ICMP packet on a tap device:

  LOCAL_ADDR="$(ip -j -4 addr show|jq -rM '.[] | .addr_info[0] | select(.scope == "global").local')"

  while :; do
  	./pasta --config-net -p pasta.pcap -u 1337 socat UDP4-LISTEN:1337,null-eof OPEN:tmp.out,create,trunc &
  	sleep 0.2 || sleep 1
  	socat OPEN:tmp.in UDP4:${LOCAL_ADDR}:1337,shut-null
  	wait
  	cmp tmp.in tmp.out
  done

Once this fails:

  tmp.in tmp.out differ: char 8193, line 29

we can finally have a look at what's going on:

  $ tshark -r pasta.pcap
      1   0.000000           :: ? ff02::16     ICMPv6 110 Multicast Listener Report Message v2
      2   0.168690 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
      3   0.168767 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
      4   0.168806 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
      5   0.168827 c6:47:05:8d:dc:04 ? Broadcast    ARP 42 Who has 88.198.0.161? Tell 88.198.0.164
      6   0.168851 9a:55:9a:55:9a:55 ? c6:47:05:8d:dc:04 ARP 42 88.198.0.161 is at 9a:55:9a:55:9a:55
      7   0.168875 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
      8   0.168896 88.198.0.164 ? 88.198.0.161 ICMP 590 Destination unreachable (Port unreachable)
      9   0.168926 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
     10   0.168959 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 8234 60260 ? 1337 Len=8192
     11   0.168989 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 4138 60260 ? 1337 Len=4096
     12   0.169010 88.198.0.161 ? 88.198.0.164 UDP 42 60260 ? 1337 Len=0

On the third datagram received, the network namespace of the container
initiates an ARP lookup to deliver the ICMP message.

In another variant of this reproducer, starting the client with:

  strace -f pasta --config-net -u 1337 socat UDP4-LISTEN:1337,null-eof OPEN:tmp.out,create,tru

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) component. The `fuse_try_move_folio()` function, responsible for managing page cache folios, fails to re-lock a request after initially unlocking it on a successful path. This oversight allows another function, `fuse_chan_abort()`, to prematurely free critical input/output arguments (`fuse_io_args`). Consequently, subsequent operations attempting to access these freed arguments can lead to a use-after-free vulnerability, potentially allowing an attacker to cause a system crash or execute arbitrary code.

notes.text: kernel: fuse: re-lock request before replacing page cache folio
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires local access and relies on winning a race condition during concurrent abort operations on user-space filesystem requests. An unprivileged local user must have permissions to interact with or mount a FUSE filesystem to initiate the conflicting input/output transactions. Successful exploitation could destabilize kernel memory, resulting in a system crash or potential privilege escalation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `net/handshake` component. A race condition exists where a network handshake request can be removed and its associated file reference released concurrently while the accept-side code attempts to access it. This can lead to the system attempting to read from freed memory or a null pointer, potentially causing system instability or a denial of service.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as a Moderate impact because successfully triggering the underlying race condition requires precise race timing during handshake cancellations, limiting exposure primarily to a local denial of service. The affected kernel handshake subsystem is engaged when kernel-layer TLS facilities (such as RPC-with-TLS) handle connection negotiation with user-space daemons. Standard enterprise deployments that do not actively utilize in-kernel transport encryption handshakes will not invoke the affected code paths.

cwe.name: Expired Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's USB subsystem (usbfs). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb node could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability. This occurs because the usb_device structure is prematurely freed before all pending operations are completed. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a system crash or potentially privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: usb: usbfs: fix use-after-free of usb_device in usbdev_release()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel usbfs (USB user-space) subsystem, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other Red Hat products that ship the Red Hat kernel. In usbdev_release(), the reference to the struct usb_device is dropped before the list of completed asynchronous URBs is drained, and the drain path (free_async() calling dec_usb_memory_use_count()) then reads back through the already-freed device, for example via bus_to_hcd(ps->dev->bus). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb device node could mmap() the file descriptor, submit an asynchronous URB whose buffer lies inside that mapping, wait for the device to be unplugged so that the usbfs reference becomes the last reference and the device is freed, and then unmap and close the file descriptor, deterministically triggering the use-after-free. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a kernel crash (denial of service) or potentially privilege escalation. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): although triggering the use-after-free itself is deterministic and not a race, reliably converting it into privilege escalation requires high attack complexity. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat products.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Server Message Block (SMB) client. When a file with the setuid or setgid bit is written to on certain Common Internet File System (CIFS) mounts (specifically those using 'cifsacl', 'modefromsid' options, or SMB3.1.1 POSIX extensions), the kernel fails to properly clear these bits on the server. This oversight allows the setuid/setgid bits to persist, which could enable a local attacker to achieve unexpected privilege escalation upon subsequent execution of the affected file.

Mount SMB/CIFS shares with the `nosuid` mount option to prevent setuid and setgid binaries from executing with elevated permissions, or prevent the `cifs` module from loading if network SMB shares are not needed.

1. Apply `nosuid` to an active mount point:
```
mount -o remount,nosuid /path/to/cifs/mount
```

2. Persist this setting by ensuring `nosuid` is present in the mount options within `/etc/fstab`:
```
//server/share /mnt/cifs cifs credentials=/etc/samba/creds,nosuid 0 0
```

3. Alternatively, if CIFS mounts are not required on the system, disable autoloading of the kernel module:
```
echo "install cifs /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/cifs.conf
```

Caveats:
Enforcing `nosuid` prevents any executable located on the mount point from running with elevated setuid or setgid privileges. Blacklisting the `cifs` module prevents all SMB/CIFS network file systems from mounting. Remounting filesystems can disrupt ongoing read and write operations.

cwe.name: Expired Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's vfio/pci component. During device initialization, a memory pointer is not properly cleared after being freed, leading to a use-after-free and double-free vulnerability. A local attacker could exploit this flaw to cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: vfio/pci: clear vdev->msi_perm after freeing it on init failure
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free and double-free flaw in the Linux kernel's vfio/pci subsystem has been rated Important by Red Hat. When initialization of the per-device MSI permission table fails (for example, when an underlying allocation fails with -ENOMEM), the error path in vfio_msi_cap_len() frees vdev->msi_perm but leaves the dangling pointer stored in the per-device vfio_pci_core_device structure, which persists across open/close cycles. A local attacker with access to a VFIO PCI device could trigger this failed initialization path and then, on a subsequent open or close of the device, cause the freed object to be reused for MSI config-space accesses (dereferencing and calling the freed perm->readfn/perm->writefn function pointers) or to be freed a second time in vfio_config_free(). This can lead to a kernel panic and system crash (denial of service) or potentially to execution of arbitrary code with elevated privileges. Red Hat rates this flaw as Important with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H); the higher CVE.org score of 8.8 reflects a lower attack-complexity assessment, whereas Red Hat considers exploitation to depend on reliably steering a memory-allocation failure during device initialization. Within Red Hat's affected product scope, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 and 7 (kernel and kernel-rt ELS streams) are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present, while the vulnerable code is present in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 (kernel and kernel-rt), Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and Red Hat OpenShift versions that ship an affected kernel, and fixes are being pursued through the responsible engineering teams.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's encrypted keys subsystem. An integer overflow occurs during memory size calculations for key data, resulting in an undersized buffer allocation. A local user can exploit this issue by supplying crafted key data to trigger an out-of-bounds write to kernel memory. This flaw can lead to a system crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS), or potentially allow privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: KEYS: encrypted: fix integer overflow of datablob_len
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security rates this flaw as IMPORTANT for the affected Red Hat products. A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's encrypted keys subsystem: encrypted_key_alloc() stores datablob_len in a u16 that is computed from multiple string and payload lengths, and when the computed length exceeds U16_MAX the stored value is truncated, resulting in an undersized buffer allocation. A slab-out-of-bounds write then occurs when __ekey_init() copies the key data into the undersized buffer. A local user able to create keys, for example via the add_key() syscall, can supply crafted key data to trigger this out-of-bounds write to kernel memory, which can cause a system crash and denial of service, or potentially allow privilege escalation. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 Extended Lifecycle Support is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that stream. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 ELS, 8, 9, and 10 (kernel and kernel-rt) and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2 (kernel and kernel-ivos-qualcomm) are affected, and fixes are being pursued for these products. Red Hat has assigned this flaw a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), reflecting a local attack vector with high attack complexity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's netfilter subsystem. In the flowtable component, connection tracking reference counts are prematurely released before flow entries are fully removed from memory. An attacker could exploit this timing issue during network flow processing, triggering a use-after-free condition. This issue primarily leads to a Denial of Service (DoS) via a system crash or unexpected system instability.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: netfilter: flowtable: hold reference on ct until flow is released
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's netfilter flowtable, affecting the kernel, kernel-rt, and kpatch packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and OpenShift Container Platform through its RHEL CoreOS components. The flowtable datapath released its connection tracking reference prematurely: nf_ct_put() frees the ct extension area immediately, and the RCU typesafe semantics could allow the datapath to refer to the wrong or already-freed conntrack entry while a flow entry was still being released after the RCU grace period. An attacker able to trigger this timing window during network flow processing could cause a use-after-free condition that primarily results in a denial of service via a system crash or unexpected system instability. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), reflecting the high attack complexity of reliably triggering the timing issue, whereas the upstream CVEORG score is 7.8 (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 and 7 Extended Life Cycle Support streams (kernel and kernel-rt) are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in those kernels. Fixes for the affected product streams are being pursued.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) component. The `fuse_try_move_folio()` function, responsible for managing page cache folios, fails to re-lock a request after initially unlocking it on a successful path. This oversight allows another function, `fuse_chan_abort()`, to prematurely free critical input/output arguments (`fuse_io_args`). Consequently, subsequent operations attempting to access these freed arguments can lead to a use-after-free vulnerability, potentially allowing an attacker to cause a system crash or execute arbitrary code.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires local access and relies on winning a race condition during concurrent abort operations on user-space filesystem requests. An unprivileged local user must have permissions to interact with or mount a FUSE filesystem to initiate the conflicting input/output transactions. Successful exploitation could destabilize kernel memory, resulting in a system crash or potential privilege escalation.

cwe.name: Expired Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. This use-after-free vulnerability exists in the `net/iucv` component. When a peer severs a connection, message notifications that still reference the freed connection path remain in a queue. A subsequent attempt to process these stale notifications can lead to memory corruption, potentially resulting in a system crash (denial of service) or allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net/iucv: fix use-after-free of a severed iucv_path
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's net/iucv (AF_IUCV socket) implementation, rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security. The af_iucv implementation queues not-yet-received message notifications on a per-socket message queue, with each notification holding a raw pointer to the connection's iucv_path. When a peer severs the connection, iucv_sever_path() frees that path but leaves the queued notifications in place; a later recvmsg() drains the queue via iucv_process_message_q() and hands the stale pointer to message_receive(), resulting in a use-after-free of the freed iucv_path. A local attacker able to open and use AF_IUCV sockets could race a peer severing the connection against processing of the queued messages, causing kernel memory corruption that can result in a system crash (denial of service) or, potentially, execution of arbitrary code. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 (kernel and kernel-rt) and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS are affected; fixes are being pursued through the respective kernel teams for the affected product streams. Red Hat Product Security scored this flaw CVSS 3.1 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), lower than the upstream CVEORG score of 8.8 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N), because successful exploitation requires local access with the ability to create AF_IUCV socket connections and depends on high attack complexity due to the timing-sensitive race between connection severing and message queue processing.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's USB subsystem (usbfs). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb node could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability. This occurs because the usb_device structure is prematurely freed before all pending operations are completed. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a system crash or potentially privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: usb: usbfs: fix use-after-free of usb_device in usbdev_release()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel usbfs (USB user-space) subsystem, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other Red Hat products that ship the Red Hat kernel. In usbdev_release(), the reference to the struct usb_device is dropped before the list of completed asynchronous URBs is drained, and the drain path (free_async() calling dec_usb_memory_use_count()) then reads back through the already-freed device, for example via bus_to_hcd(ps->dev->bus). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb device node could mmap() the file descriptor, submit an asynchronous URB whose buffer lies inside that mapping, wait for the device to be unplugged so that the usbfs reference becomes the last reference and the device is freed, and then unmap and close the file descriptor, deterministically triggering the use-after-free. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a kernel crash (denial of service) or potentially privilege escalation. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): although triggering the use-after-free itself is deterministic and not a race, reliably converting it into privilege escalation requires high attack complexity. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat products.

cwe.name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV (Advanced Program-to-Program Communication over IUCV) network protocol implementation. The `afiucv_hs_rcv()` function, responsible for receiving frames, does not properly filter incoming frames based on the ingress network device. This oversight allows a local attacker with specific network capabilities or a host on the same HiperSockets segment to send specially crafted frames. Successful exploitation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting the accept-queue, injecting data into existing sockets, and disrupting established connections.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net/iucv: filter frames in afiucv_hs_rcv() by ingress device
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV protocol implementation, used for the z/VM IUCV and HiperSockets transports on the s390x (IBM Z) architecture. The afiucv_hs_rcv() receive path selected a target socket from the global socket list by matching only the four 8-byte name fields in the frame's transport header, without checking the network device the frame arrived on. As a result, a frame received on any network device could be delivered to an AF_IUCV socket bound to a different device or to the classic z/VM IUCV transport. A local attacker holding only the CAP_NET_RAW capability inside an unprivileged user and network namespace could send a raw ETH_P_AF_IUCV frame on its own loopback device and have it matched against sockets in the initial network namespace; similarly, a host on the same shared HiperSockets segment could direct frames at sockets bound to a different HiperSockets device. Successful exploitation could exhaust a listening socket's accept queue (denial of service), inject data into existing AF_IUCV connections, control the peer identity of accepted child sockets, and disrupt or kill established connections. Multiple Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernel and kernel-rt update streams and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS kernel streams are affected, and fixes are being pursued in the respective product streams; the kernel-ivos-qualcomm component of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that kernel. The Red Hat severity of IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1 score 7.0, AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) is lower than the upstream CVE.org rating of 8.1 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N): Red Hat assessed the dominant exploitation path as local, requiring privileges and high attack complexity, whereas the upstream rating emphasizes the adjacent-network HiperSockets vector requiring no privileges. Note that AF_IUCV over HiperSockets provides no per-connection authentication, so the fix reduces the attack surface to peers present on the same HiperSockets segment but does not change that protocol-level property.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Server Message Block (SMB) client. When a file with the setuid or setgid bit is written to on certain Common Internet File System (CIFS) mounts (specifically those using 'cifsacl', 'modefromsid' options, or SMB3.1.1 POSIX extensions), the kernel fails to properly clear these bits on the server. This oversight allows the setuid/setgid bits to persist, which could enable a local attacker to achieve unexpected privilege escalation upon subsequent execution of the affected file.

Mount SMB/CIFS shares with the `nosuid` mount option to prevent setuid and setgid binaries from executing with elevated permissions, or prevent the `cifs` module from loading if network SMB shares are not needed.

1. Apply `nosuid` to an active mount point:
```
mount -o remount,nosuid /path/to/cifs/mount
```

2. Persist this setting by ensuring `nosuid` is present in the mount options within `/etc/fstab`:
```
//server/share /mnt/cifs cifs credentials=/etc/samba/creds,nosuid 0 0
```

3. Alternatively, if CIFS mounts are not required on the system, disable autoloading of the kernel module:
```
echo "install cifs /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/cifs.conf
```

Caveats:
Enforcing `nosuid` prevents any executable located on the mount point from running with elevated setuid or setgid privileges. Blacklisting the `cifs` module prevents all SMB/CIFS network file systems from mounting. Remounting filesystems can disrupt ongoing read and write operations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

net0: index=0,type=nic,model=virtio-net-pci,macaddr=52:54:00:12:34:57

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) component. The `fuse_try_move_folio()` function, responsible for managing page cache folios, fails to re-lock a request after initially unlocking it on a successful path. This oversight allows another function, `fuse_chan_abort()`, to prematurely free critical input/output arguments (`fuse_io_args`). Consequently, subsequent operations attempting to access these freed arguments can lead to a use-after-free vulnerability, potentially allowing an attacker to cause a system crash or execute arbitrary code.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires local access and relies on winning a race condition during concurrent abort operations on user-space filesystem requests. An unprivileged local user must have permissions to interact with or mount a FUSE filesystem to initiate the conflicting input/output transactions. Successful exploitation could destabilize kernel memory, resulting in a system crash or potential privilege escalation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Generic Receive Offload (GRO) networking subsystem. An attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted network packets that cause a double aggregation of flush-marked socket buffers (skbs). This issue arises from a missing flush check, which allows already-processed packets to be re-aggregated, corrupting the internal data structure. This corruption leads to an invalid state when the system attempts to process these packets, triggering a kernel panic and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. This use-after-free vulnerability exists in the `net/iucv` component. When a peer severs a connection, message notifications that still reference the freed connection path remain in a queue. A subsequent attempt to process these stale notifications can lead to memory corruption, potentially resulting in a system crash (denial of service) or allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net/iucv: fix use-after-free of a severed iucv_path
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's net/iucv (AF_IUCV socket) implementation, rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security. The af_iucv implementation queues not-yet-received message notifications on a per-socket message queue, with each notification holding a raw pointer to the connection's iucv_path. When a peer severs the connection, iucv_sever_path() frees that path but leaves the queued notifications in place; a later recvmsg() drains the queue via iucv_process_message_q() and hands the stale pointer to message_receive(), resulting in a use-after-free of the freed iucv_path. A local attacker able to open and use AF_IUCV sockets could race a peer severing the connection against processing of the queued messages, causing kernel memory corruption that can result in a system crash (denial of service) or, potentially, execution of arbitrary code. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 (kernel and kernel-rt) and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS are affected; fixes are being pursued through the respective kernel teams for the affected product streams. Red Hat Product Security scored this flaw CVSS 3.1 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), lower than the upstream CVEORG score of 8.8 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N), because successful exploitation requires local access with the ability to create AF_IUCV socket connections and depends on high attack complexity due to the timing-sensitive race between connection severing and message queue processing.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's IP Virtual Server (IPVS) module. When processing network packets, a buffer reallocation can leave an IP header pointer referencing freed memory. An attacker could exploit this use-after-free condition to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the system or potentially corrupt system memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipvs: reload ip header after head reallocation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as Important rather than Moderate because improper memory handling during packet processing can lead to kernel memory corruption or an abrupt system crash. The issue specifically affects environments running IP Virtual Server (IPVS) functionality, which is not enabled or loaded by default across standard installations. The vulnerability affects the Multipath TCP (MPTCP) feature in the Linux kernel. To mitigate this issue, MPTCP can be disabled by preventing the `mptcp` kernel module from loading. To disable the `mptcp` module: 1. Create a new file `/etc/modprobe.d/disable-mptcp.conf` with the following content: `install mptcp /bin/true
blacklist mptcp` 2. Regenerate the initramfs to ensure the change takes effect on boot: `sudo dracut -f -v` 3. Reboot the system for the changes to take effect. Disabling MPTCP may impact network performance or functionality for applications that rely on Multipath TCP.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's USB subsystem (usbfs). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb node could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability. This occurs because the usb_device structure is prematurely freed before all pending operations are completed. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a system crash or potentially privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: usb: usbfs: fix use-after-free of usb_device in usbdev_release()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel usbfs (USB user-space) subsystem, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other Red Hat products that ship the Red Hat kernel. In usbdev_release(), the reference to the struct usb_device is dropped before the list of completed asynchronous URBs is drained, and the drain path (free_async() calling dec_usb_memory_use_count()) then reads back through the already-freed device, for example via bus_to_hcd(ps->dev->bus). An unprivileged local attacker with read/write access to a /dev/bus/usb device node could mmap() the file descriptor, submit an asynchronous URB whose buffer lies inside that mapping, wait for the device to be unplugged so that the usbfs reference becomes the last reference and the device is freed, and then unmap and close the file descriptor, deterministically triggering the use-after-free. Successful exploitation of this memory corruption flaw could lead to a kernel crash (denial of service) or potentially privilege escalation. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): although triggering the use-after-free itself is deterministic and not a race, reliably converting it into privilege escalation requires high attack complexity. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat products.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV (Advanced Program-to-Program Communication over IUCV) network protocol implementation. The `afiucv_hs_rcv()` function, responsible for receiving frames, does not properly filter incoming frames based on the ingress network device. This oversight allows a local attacker with specific network capabilities or a host on the same HiperSockets segment to send specially crafted frames. Successful exploitation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting the accept-queue, injecting data into existing sockets, and disrupting established connections.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net/iucv: filter frames in afiucv_hs_rcv() by ingress device
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV protocol implementation, used for the z/VM IUCV and HiperSockets transports on the s390x (IBM Z) architecture. The afiucv_hs_rcv() receive path selected a target socket from the global socket list by matching only the four 8-byte name fields in the frame's transport header, without checking the network device the frame arrived on. As a result, a frame received on any network device could be delivered to an AF_IUCV socket bound to a different device or to the classic z/VM IUCV transport. A local attacker holding only the CAP_NET_RAW capability inside an unprivileged user and network namespace could send a raw ETH_P_AF_IUCV frame on its own loopback device and have it matched against sockets in the initial network namespace; similarly, a host on the same shared HiperSockets segment could direct frames at sockets bound to a different HiperSockets device. Successful exploitation could exhaust a listening socket's accept queue (denial of service), inject data into existing AF_IUCV connections, control the peer identity of accepted child sockets, and disrupt or kill established connections. Multiple Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernel and kernel-rt update streams and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS kernel streams are affected, and fixes are being pursued in the respective product streams; the kernel-ivos-qualcomm component of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that kernel. The Red Hat severity of IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1 score 7.0, AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) is lower than the upstream CVE.org rating of 8.1 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N): Red Hat assessed the dominant exploitation path as local, requiring privileges and high attack complexity, whereas the upstream rating emphasizes the adjacent-network HiperSockets vector requiring no privileges. Note that AF_IUCV over HiperSockets provides no per-connection authentication, so the fix reduces the attack surface to peers present on the same HiperSockets segment but does not change that protocol-level property.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Server Message Block (SMB) client. When a file with the setuid or setgid bit is written to on certain Common Internet File System (CIFS) mounts (specifically those using 'cifsacl', 'modefromsid' options, or SMB3.1.1 POSIX extensions), the kernel fails to properly clear these bits on the server. This oversight allows the setuid/setgid bits to persist, which could enable a local attacker to achieve unexpected privilege escalation upon subsequent execution of the affected file.

Mount SMB/CIFS shares with the `nosuid` mount option to prevent setuid and setgid binaries from executing with elevated permissions, or prevent the `cifs` module from loading if network SMB shares are not needed.

1. Apply `nosuid` to an active mount point:
```
mount -o remount,nosuid /path/to/cifs/mount
```

2. Persist this setting by ensuring `nosuid` is present in the mount options within `/etc/fstab`:
```
//server/share /mnt/cifs cifs credentials=/etc/samba/creds,nosuid 0 0
```

3. Alternatively, if CIFS mounts are not required on the system, disable autoloading of the kernel module:
```
echo "install cifs /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/cifs.conf
```

Caveats:
Enforcing `nosuid` prevents any executable located on the mount point from running with elevated setuid or setgid privileges. Blacklisting the `cifs` module prevents all SMB/CIFS network file systems from mounting. Remounting filesystems can disrupt ongoing read and write operations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s TLS implementation (net/tls/tls_device.c). The function get_netdev_for_sock() is invoked during setsockopt(), which is not executed under RCU (Read-Copy-Update) protection. It previously used sk_dst_get(sk)->dev, which can lead to a use-after-free (UAF) if the sk’s destination is freed
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: tls: Use __sk_dst_get() and dst_dev_rcu() in get_netdev_for_sock()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because exploiting this race condition requires local socket manipulation and specific timing to trigger the use-after-free condition, typically leading to a system crash (denial of service) rather than arbitrary code execution. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, kernel TLS device offload functionality is not widely enabled by default and requires explicit socket configuration by local processes. Consequently, the practical risk is constrained to local denial of service under specific concurrency conditions.

cwe.name: Race Condition within a Thread

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's qla2xxx SCSI driver. This vulnerability occurs when commands sent to the firmware (FW) are not properly cleared after a chip reset. A local attacker could exploit a race condition during direct memory access (DMA) unmapping, leading to a kernel panic. This can result in a system crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: Linux kernel: Denial of Service in qla2xxx SCSI driver due to improper command handling after chip reset
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate flaw was found in the Linux kernel's qla2xxx SCSI driver, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt components in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10. Commands sent to the firmware were not properly cleared after a chip reset, and a race condition between two CPUs concurrently performing DMA unmapping in qlt_unmap_sg() could trigger a kernel BUG_ON, resulting in a kernel panic. A local attacker able to trigger the chip reset and racing DMA unmap paths could exploit this condition to crash the system, causing a denial of service; confidentiality and integrity are not impacted. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 1 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in those releases. Fixes for the affected Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 streams are being pursued by the Red Hat kernel team, and updates have already shipped or are in progress for several streams. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity with a CVSS 4.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), which differs significantly from the Critical 9.8 score in the upstream CVE record. The upstream score reflects a network-reachable vector with full confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact that is not supported by the technical evidence: exploitation requires local access and a high-complexity race condition, and only availability is affected.

To mitigate this issue, if the `qla2xxx` SCSI driver is not required, it can be prevented from loading by blacklisting the module. This can be achieved by creating a modprobe configuration file.

1. Create a file named `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-qla2xxx.conf` with the following content:
```
blacklist qla2xxx
install qla2xxx /bin/true
```
2. Rebuild the initial ramdisk:
```bash
dracut -f -v
```
3. Reboot the system for the changes to take effect.

This mitigation will prevent the `qla2xxx` module from loading, which may impact systems relying on QLogic Fibre Channel HBAs. A system reboot is required for the changes to take full effect.

cwe.name: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `drm/xe` component of the Linux kernel. This vulnerability involves insufficient protection of Graphics Translation Table (GGTT) Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) access. When the driver fails to load or during certain cleanup operations, the system's memory access protection is inadequate. This could allow a local attacker to potentially cause the system to become unstable or unresponsive, leading to a denial of service.

cwe.name: Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's drm/xe driver. During 3D workload processing, a user process can trigger an issue in the Virtual Memory Area (VMA) management when performing a rebind operation. This can lead to an invalid or overlapping VMA insertion, causing the system to enter an unstable state and potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: drm/xe: always keep track of remap prev/next
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw with MODERATE impact was found in the Linux kernel's Intel xe graphics driver (drm/xe) as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. While processing VM bind operations issued by a user-space 3D workload, a rebind that splits an existing virtual memory area (VMA) can skip rebinding already-compatible end segments and shrink the original unmap range accordingly. If the bind operation subsequently fails and takes the unwind path, the driver can re-insert a VMA that overlaps those still-present end segments, triggering a kernel WARNING in vm_bind_ioctl_ops_unwind and leaving the GPU virtual memory state inconsistent. A local user able to run graphics workloads can use this to destabilize or crash the kernel, resulting in a denial of service. The vulnerable code entered Red Hat Enterprise Linux with the DRM changes merged from upstream Linux v6.7..v6.8, so Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, and 8, as well as the RHEL 9.0, 9.2, and 9.4 update streams, are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 and later update streams, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2 are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the standard update process for those products. Red Hat's MODERATE rating differs from the higher upstream CVE.org severity because exploitation requires local access and the established failure mode is denial of service.

cwe.name: Incorrect Synchronization

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `smbdirect` module. A race condition in the receive credit management logic allows the system to grant credits that a peer has already consumed. This timing vulnerability, occurring during the processing of incoming data, could lead to resource exhaustion and potentially result in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: smb: smbdirect: introduce smbdirect_socket.recv_io.credits.available
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate because exploitation requires an established SMB Direct session over RDMA-capable networking, restricting the potential impact to denial of service without permitting unauthorized code execution. SMB Direct is not enabled or utilized by default in standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments and requires explicit administrator configuration alongside compatible RDMA hardware. Consequently, systems not actively running SMB over RDMA transports are not exposed to this race condition.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) implementation. This vulnerability, a use-after-free, occurs when the system processes a Stale Cookie ERROR during the setup or reconfiguration of an SCTP association. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted SCTP packets. This could lead to a system crash, causing a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: sctp: purge outqueue on stale COOKIE-ECHO handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use after free can occur in the SCTP stale COOKIE-ECHO handling path when a Stale Cookie ERROR rolls an association back from COOKIE_ECHOED to COOKIE_WAIT while user data is already queued or bundled with COOKIE-ECHO. The stream update path can free the old stream state, while scheduler cached state such as stream out_curr or queued transmit state can still reference the freed sctp_stream_out entry. Later SCTP dequeue paths such as FCFS, RR, or PRIO may dereference the stale stream state and crash the kernel. The issue is network reachable but AC:H is used because the trigger depends on a specific association setup and stale cookie rollback sequence. Impact is remote denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's IPv6 Virtual Tunnel Interface (vti6) component. An unprivileged local user, particularly within a user namespace, could exploit a vulnerability related to incorrect network namespace handling during the movement of a vti6 tunnel. This issue can lead to a kernel bug, resulting in a denial of service (system crash) and potentially impacting container isolation on affected hosts.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ip6: vti: Use ip6_tnl.net in vti6_changelink()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A stale per-network-namespace VTI6 tunnel entry can remain after a VTI6 device is moved between network namespaces because the update and changelink paths use the device's current network namespace instead of the tunnel's original namespace. When the original namespace is later destroyed, `cleanup_net()` may access the stale entry after the associated object has been freed, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

The vulnerability is considered to require low privileges (PR:L) because an unprivileged local user can reach the affected code path by creating user and network namespaces and obtaining the required capabilities within the newly created user namespace, where unprivileged user namespaces are enabled. Host-level `CAP_NET_ADMIN` is therefore not required. The issue is not remotely exploitable through network traffic; exploitation requires local netlink and network-namespace operations.

Successful exploitation can cause a kernel crash and host-wide denial of service. Because the underlying flaw is a kernel use-after-free, confidentiality and integrity impacts may also be possible, although privilege escalation has not been demonstrated. The practical impact can be greater on container hosts because an unprivileged workload with access to user and network namespaces may trigger the flaw in the shared host kernel, potentially affecting other containers or tenants outside the attacker's own namespace.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's xfrm input component. The transport-mode reinjection process, which handles network packet re-injection, stores a network namespace pointer that must remain valid until a deferred callback completes. However, a missing reference count for the network namespace during this deferred operation could lead to a use-after-free vulnerability. This could allow an attacker to potentially cause a system crash or other unpredictable behavior if the network namespace is deallocated prematurely.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: xfrm: input: hold netns during deferred transport reinjection

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires local access and precise timing to trigger a race condition during network namespace termination. The flaw stems from improper reference counting during deferred IPsec packet processing, which can allow an authenticated local user to cause a kernel crash or memory corruption. The high execution complexity and reliance on concurrent namespace destruction prevent reliable remote exploitation. Older releases such as Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected as the relevant subsystem changes were introduced in later kernel baselines.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's IPv6 Virtual Tunnel Interface (VTI) module. When a VTI tunnel device is moved to a different network environment, an unprivileged user in a separate user space can manipulate tunnel parameters. This manipulation could allow the user to intercept or redirect network traffic intended for other parts of the system or other containers, leading to unauthorized information disclosure or denial of service across different tenants on a container host.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because unprivileged local attackers operating inside containers can cross tenant boundaries and hijack traffic routing in shared hosting environments. By taking advantage of unprivileged user and network namespaces enabled by default on standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux installations, an attacker can misroute tunnel packets from the initial namespace. While exploitation requires local execution within a namespace rather than direct remote access, the resulting cross-tenant network disruption and eavesdropping justify the Important classification over a lower severity level.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Security Module (LSM). A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by leveraging an improper handling of a credential guard mutex in the `lsm_set_self_attr()` function. This oversight may allow the attacker to bypass security restrictions enforced by modules such as SELinux and AppArmor when a process is being debugged, potentially leading to unauthorized access or privilege escalation.

Earlier enterprise distributions, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, are unaffected because they do not include the newer LSM system call interfaces. On affected platforms, an authenticated local attacker might bypass policy transition controls enforced by mandatory access control frameworks such as SELinux.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's drm/xe/pt module. During certain memory management operations, an internal counter is not properly reset. Repeated attempts to perform these operations, possibly due to resource contention or out-of-memory conditions, can cause this counter to exceed its allocated bounds. This leads to an out-of-bounds write and a subsequent use-after-free vulnerability, which can result in a system crash, causing a denial of service.

notes.text:
An update for kernel-rt is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The kernel-rt packages provide the Real Time Linux Kernel, which enables fine-tuning for systems with extremely high determinism requirements.

Security Fix(es):

* kernel: EDAC/bluefield: Fix potential integer overflow (CVE-2024-53161)

* kernel: wifi: mac80211: Discard Beacon frames to non-broadcast address (CVE-2025-71127)

* kernel: KVM: nSVM: Always use vmcb01 in VMLOAD/VMSAVE emulation (CVE-2026-43133)

* kernel: net: qrtr: fix refcount saturation and potential UAF in qrtr_port_remove (CVE-2026-52947)

* kernel: wifi: nl80211: reject oversized EMA RNR lists (CVE-2026-53182)

* kernel: blk-cgroup: fix UAF in __blkcg_rstat_flush() (CVE-2026-63802)

* kernel: scsi: scsi_transport_fc: Widen FPIN pname walker counter to u32 (CVE-2026-63889)

* kernel: wifi: mac80211: capture fast-RX rate before mesh reuses skb->cb (CVE-2026-64117)

* kernel: Linux kernel: ath9k Wi-Fi driver use-after-free vulnerability leading to system crash (CVE-2026-68363)

* kernel: net: qrtr: restrict socket creation to the initial network namespace (CVE-2026-68294)

* kernel: dm-verity: fix buffer overflow in FEC calculation (CVE-2026-72098)

* kernel: scsi: libiscsi_tcp: Bound SCSI Response data segment to the connection buffer (CVE-2026-74556)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

EDAC/bluefield: Fix potential integer overflow

The 64-bit argument for the "get DIMM info" SMC call consists of mem_ctrl_idx
left-shifted 16 bits and OR-ed with DIMM index.  With mem_ctrl_idx defined as
32-bits wide the left-shift operation truncates the upper 16 bits of
information during the calculation of the SMC argument.

The mem_ctrl_idx stack variable must be defined as 64-bits wide to prevent any
potential integer overflow, i.e. loss of data from upper 16 bits.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Actual only for latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (where configuration parameter CONFIG_EDAC_BLUEFIELD enabled as module). For triggering this bug need physical access (kind of insert malicious DIMM of memory), because it can happen only during boot or after DIMM of memory updated. Could happen only if this type of memory being used: "Mellanox BlueField SoC". The security impact is limited.

notes.text: A beacon protection bypass vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's mac80211 WiFi stack. According to IEEE 802.11-2020, beacon frames must be sent to the broadcast address, but mac80211 incorrectly accepts unicast beacon frames with the Protected Frame bit set to 1. This allows attackers to send targeted unicast beacons that bypass beacon protection (BIGTK verification), potentially forcing associated stations to perform malicious actions like channel switching via CSA.

notes.text: This vulnerability affects WiFi clients using mac80211-based drivers. An attacker within wireless range can send crafted unicast beacon frames to target specific stations, bypassing beacon protection mechanisms. This could be used to force channel switches or other beacon-triggered behaviors. The attack requires proximity to the target WiFi network.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) nSVM module. When a nested virtual machine (L2 guest) executes VMSAVE/VMLOAD instructions, and these are not intercepted by the first-level hypervisor (L1), KVM incorrectly uses `vmcb02` instead of `vmcb01` for managing guest state. This incorrect Virtual Machine Control Block (VMCB) handling could lead to unexpected behavior or state corruption within the virtualized environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `qrtr` network subsystem. A race condition exists in the `qrtr_port_remove()` function where the socket reference count is decremented prematurely. This allows a concurrent reader to access a socket whose reference count has dropped to zero, potentially leading to a Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this to cause memory corruption, leading to system instability or a denial of service.

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate severity impact because exploitation requires local access and precise timing to trigger a race condition during Qualcomm IPC Router (QRTR) socket teardown. Although a successful exploit may lead to kernel memory corruption or system instability, the vulnerable QRTR protocol is specific to Qualcomm inter-processor communication and is typically not active in standard enterprise server environments. Furthermore, unprivileged users do not interact with this subsystem under typical deployment configurations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's block input/output control group (blk-cgroup) component. This vulnerability, a Use-After-Free (UAF), occurs when multiple block control groups are released at the same time. cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Fibre Channel (FC) transport component. An adjacent Fibre Channel fabric actor, such as a compromised switch or fabric controller, can send a specially crafted FPIN ELS (Fabric Performance Incentive Notification Extended Link Service) frame. This malformed frame, specifically with a `pname_count` field that causes an integer overflow, can trigger an infinite loop, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) in the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: scsi: scsi_transport_fc: Widen FPIN pname walker counter to u32
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires direct access to an adjacent Fibre Channel storage fabric rather than a general IP or local network interface. Systems are only vulnerable if configured with Fibre Channel host bus adapters connecting to an untrusted or compromised storage area network. While successfully triggering the infinite loop results in an unresponsive kernel and host-level denial of service, the prerequisite of fabric-level access or malicious switch control limits the overall blast radius across typical server deployments.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's mac80211 Wi-Fi subsystem. This use-after-free vulnerability arises from incorrect handling of fast-RX rate data during mesh processing. This can lead to memory corruption, which an attacker could potentially exploit to cause a system crash (denial of service) or, in some cases, execute unauthorized code.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: wifi: mac80211: capture fast-RX rate before mesh reuses skb->cb
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this issue as having a Moderate security impact because successful exploitation requires wireless hardware actively configured in an 802.11s mesh network forwarding topology. Wireless interfaces and mesh routing are uncommon in typical enterprise server deployments, substantially limiting exposure under default configurations. Where mesh forwarding is operational, an attacker within adjacent radio range could trigger the invalid memory reference, potentially causing a kernel panic or unauthorized privilege escalation.

cwe.name: Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's QRTR (Qualcomm IPC Router) networking component. An unprivileged local attacker can create a QRTR socket in a separate network namespace. Due to improper handling of global state variables, this allows the attacker to send datagrams and control-plane messages to QRTR sockets in other network namespaces. This bypasses network namespace isolation, enabling unauthorized communication and potential information disclosure between isolated network environments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the ath9k Wi-Fi driver in the Linux kernel. A race condition exists during the asynchronous firmware loading process and device disconnection. This could lead to reading freed memory, potentially causing a system crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `libiscsi_tcp` component. A remote attacker, acting as a malicious iSCSI target, could send a specially crafted iSCSI SCSI Command Response (ISCSI_OP_SCSI_CMD_RSP) with an oversized data segment.
