cwe.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

notes.text:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

EDAC/bluefield: Fix potential integer overflow

The 64-bit argument for the "get DIMM info" SMC call consists of mem_ctrl_idx
left-shifted 16 bits and OR-ed with DIMM index.  With mem_ctrl_idx defined as
32-bits wide the left-shift operation truncates the upper 16 bits of
information during the calculation of the SMC argument.

The mem_ctrl_idx stack variable must be defined as 64-bits wide to prevent any
potential integer overflow, i.e. loss of data from upper 16 bits.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: EDAC/bluefield: Fix potential integer overflow
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Actual only for latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (where configuration parameter CONFIG_EDAC_BLUEFIELD enabled as module). For triggering this bug need physical access (kind of insert malicious DIMM of memory), because it can happen only during boot or after DIMM of memory updated. Could happen only if this type of memory being used: "Mellanox BlueField SoC". The security impact is limited.

notes.text: A beacon protection bypass vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's mac80211 WiFi stack. According to IEEE 802.11-2020, beacon frames must be sent to the broadcast address, but mac80211 incorrectly accepts unicast beacon frames with the Protected Frame bit set to 1. This allows attackers to send targeted unicast beacons that bypass beacon protection (BIGTK verification), potentially forcing associated stations to perform malicious actions like channel switching via CSA.

notes.text: This vulnerability affects WiFi clients using mac80211-based drivers. An attacker within wireless range can send crafted unicast beacon frames to target specific stations, bypassing beacon protection mechanisms. This could be used to force channel switches or other beacon-triggered behaviors. The attack requires proximity to the target WiFi network.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) nSVM module. When a nested virtual machine (L2 guest) executes VMSAVE/VMLOAD instructions, and these are not intercepted by the first-level hypervisor (L1), KVM incorrectly uses `vmcb02` instead of `vmcb01` for managing guest state. This incorrect Virtual Machine Control Block (VMCB) handling could lead to unexpected behavior or state corruption within the virtualized environment.

cwe.name: Improper Update of Reference Count

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's `qrtr` network subsystem. A race condition exists in the `qrtr_port_remove()` function where the socket reference count is decremented prematurely. This allows a concurrent reader to access a socket whose reference count has dropped to zero, potentially leading to a Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this to cause memory corruption, leading to system instability or a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate severity impact because exploitation requires local access and precise timing to trigger a race condition during Qualcomm IPC Router (QRTR) socket teardown. Although a successful exploit may lead to kernel memory corruption or system instability, the vulnerable QRTR protocol is specific to Qualcomm inter-processor communication and is typically not active in standard enterprise server environments. Furthermore, unprivileged users do not interact with this subsystem under typical deployment configurations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's nl80211 Wi-Fi subsystem. The nl80211_parse_rnr_elems() function, responsible for parsing EMA RNR (Enhanced Multiple Access Reduced Neighbor Report) lists, does not properly handle an excessive number of nested NL80211_ATTR_EMA_RNR_ELEMS inputs. This improper input validation could allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) by providing an oversized EMA RNR list, potentially leading to system instability or a crash.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's block input/output control group (blk-cgroup) component. This vulnerability, a Use-After-Free (UAF), occurs when multiple block control groups are released at the same time. A race condition allows one group to remove another's entries while it is still in use, leading to premature memory deallocation. This can result in system instability or a denial of service.

cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Fibre Channel (FC) transport component. An adjacent Fibre Channel fabric actor, such as a compromised switch or fabric controller, can send a specially crafted FPIN ELS (Fabric Performance Incentive Notification Extended Link Service) frame. This malformed frame, specifically with a `pname_count` field that causes an integer overflow, can trigger an infinite loop, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) in the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: scsi: scsi_transport_fc: Widen FPIN pname walker counter to u32
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires direct access to an adjacent Fibre Channel storage fabric rather than a general IP or local network interface. Systems are only vulnerable if configured with Fibre Channel host bus adapters connecting to an untrusted or compromised storage area network. While successfully triggering the infinite loop results in an unresponsive kernel and host-level denial of service, the prerequisite of fabric-level access or malicious switch control limits the overall blast radius across typical server deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's mac80211 Wi-Fi subsystem. This use-after-free vulnerability arises from incorrect handling of fast-RX rate data during mesh processing. This can lead to memory corruption, which an attacker could potentially exploit to cause a system crash (denial of service) or, in some cases, execute unauthorized code.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this issue as having a Moderate security impact because successful exploitation requires wireless hardware actively configured in an 802.11s mesh network forwarding topology. Wireless interfaces and mesh routing are uncommon in typical enterprise server deployments, substantially limiting exposure under default configurations. Where mesh forwarding is operational, an attacker within adjacent radio range could trigger the invalid memory reference, potentially causing a kernel panic or unauthorized privilege escalation.

* kernel: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix possible crash on l2cap_ecred_conn_rsp (CVE-2026-63975)

* kernel: Bluetooth: HIDP: fix missing length checks in hidp_input_report() (CVE-2026-63947)

* kernel: Bluetooth: hci_sync: fix UAF in hci_le_create_cis_sync (CVE-2026-63944)

* kernel: Bluetooth: ISO: fix UAF in iso_recv_frame (CVE-2026-63946)

* kernel: Bluetooth: ISO: serialize iso_sock_clear_timer with socket lock (CVE-2026-63945)

* kernel: wifi: mac80211: capture fast-RX rate before mesh reuses skb->cb (CVE-2026-64117)

* kernel: wifi: iwlwifi: mld: fix TSO segmentation explosion when AMSDU is disabled (CVE-2026-64037)

* kernel: ixgbevf: fix use-after-free in VEPA multicast source pruning (CVE-2026-64113)

* kernel: wifi: iwlwifi: mld: validate sta_mask before ffs() in BA session handlers (CVE-2026-64255)

* kernel: wifi: mac80211: fix MLE defragmentation (CVE-2026-64515)

* kernel: mm/khugepaged: write all dirty file folios when collapsing (CVE-2026-68086)

* kernel: Linux kernel: Wi-Fi subsystem out-of-bounds read via crafted frames (CVE-2026-68402)

* kernel: sctp: fix auth_hmacs array size in struct sctp_cookie (CVE-2026-68376)

* kernel: wifi: cfg80211: validate PMSR FTM preamble range (CVE-2026-68406)

* kernel: tipc: clear sock->sk on the failed-insert path in tipc_sk_create() (CVE-2026-68117)

* kernel: sctp: auth: verify auth requirement when auth_chunk is NULL (CVE-2026-68300)

* kernel: drm/xe/pt: Reset current_op in xe_pt_update_ops_init() (CVE-2026-68264)

* kernel: sctp: validate stream count in sctp_process_strreset_inreq() (CVE-2026-68315)

* kernel: dm-verity: fix buffer overflow in FEC calculation (CVE-2026-72098)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

*  gfs2: Various xfstests fixes [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-178219)

* rtla-timerlat-top doesn't stop properly when threshold is reached on multiple CPUs at once [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-193025)

* qede: build_skb failure causes off-by-one BD ring corruption and kernel panic [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-193050)

* Customer needs "netfilter: nfnetlink_queue: optimize verdict lookup with hash table" patch [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-224489)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: Race Condition within a Thread

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's qla2xxx SCSI driver. This vulnerability occurs when commands sent to the firmware (FW) are not properly cleared after a chip reset. A local attacker could exploit a race condition during direct memory access (DMA) unmapping, leading to a kernel panic. This can result in a system crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: Linux kernel: Denial of Service in qla2xxx SCSI driver due to improper command handling after chip reset
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate flaw was found in the Linux kernel's qla2xxx SCSI driver, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt components in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10. Commands sent to the firmware were not properly cleared after a chip reset, and a race condition between two CPUs concurrently performing DMA unmapping in qlt_unmap_sg() could trigger a kernel BUG_ON, resulting in a kernel panic. A local attacker able to trigger the chip reset and racing DMA unmap paths could exploit this condition to crash the system, causing a denial of service; confidentiality and integrity are not impacted. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 1 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in those releases. Fixes for the affected Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 streams are being pursued by the Red Hat kernel team, and updates have already shipped or are in progress for several streams. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity with a CVSS 4.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), which differs significantly from the Critical 9.8 score in the upstream CVE record. The upstream score reflects a network-reachable vector with full confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact that is not supported by the technical evidence: exploitation requires local access and a high-complexity race condition, and only availability is affected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

The system must be rebooted for this update to take effect.

Red Hat recommends treating all kernel errata as security-relevant. Given the kernel's fundamental role, any bug has a higher chance of impacting system security, even if that impact only becomes clear after a fix is published. Therefore, Red Hat prioritizes delivering fixes that improve our customers' overall security posture.

Because of this proactive approach, a patch may be associated with a CVE assignment at a future date. Retroactive CVE assignments are always documented in the corresponding errata and on Red Hat's CVE pages. We strongly advise against delaying updates, as doing so may leave your system exposed when protections are already available.

To mitigate this issue, if the `qla2xxx` SCSI driver is not required, it can be prevented from loading by blacklisting the module. This can be achieved by creating a modprobe configuration file.

1. Create a file named `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-qla2xxx.conf` with the following content:
```
blacklist qla2xxx
install qla2xxx /bin/true
```

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's drm/xe driver. During 3D workload processing, a user process can trigger an issue in the Virtual Memory Area (VMA) management when performing a rebind operation. This can lead to an invalid or overlapping VMA insertion, causing the system to enter an unstable state and potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: drm/xe: always keep track of remap prev/next
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw with MODERATE impact was found in the Linux kernel's Intel xe graphics driver (drm/xe) as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. While processing VM bind operations issued by a user-space 3D workload, a rebind that splits an existing virtual memory area (VMA) can skip rebinding already-compatible end segments and shrink the original unmap range accordingly. If the bind operation subsequently fails and takes the unwind path, the driver can re-insert a VMA that overlaps those still-present end segments, triggering a kernel WARNING in vm_bind_ioctl_ops_unwind and leaving the GPU virtual memory state inconsistent. A local user able to run graphics workloads can use this to destabilize or crash the kernel, resulting in a denial of service. The vulnerable code entered Red Hat Enterprise Linux with the DRM changes merged from upstream Linux v6.7..v6.8, so Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, and 8, as well as the RHEL 9.0, 9.2, and 9.4 update streams, are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 and later update streams, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2 are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the standard update process for those products. Red Hat's MODERATE rating differs from the higher upstream CVE.org severity because exploitation requires local access and the established failure mode is denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) implementation. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a specially crafted COOKIE_ECHO chunk to a listening SCTP server. The server's failure to properly validate the length of a cached peer INIT chunk within the COOKIE_ECHO payload could lead to out-of-bounds reads and memory corruption. This could result in a denial of service or potentially information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: sctp: validate cached peer INIT chunk length in COOKIE_ECHO processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: SCTP COOKIE_ECHO processing failed to validate the cached peer INIT chunk length against the remaining cookie buffer, allowing a remote SCTP peer to make parameter parsing walk beyond received data and potentially trigger OOB reads or later memory corruption in SCTP parameter handling. This allows sctp_process_init() and sctp_walk_params() to walk beyond the actual received buffer and can lead to out-of-bounds reads during later parameter handling such as STATE_COOKIE processing and kmemdup() copies.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's ixgbevf network driver. This vulnerability, a use-after-free, occurs when the driver attempts to process network packets for a specific multicast workaround. An attacker could potentially exploit this by sending specially crafted network traffic, which may lead to a system crash, resulting in a denial of service, or in some cases, could allow for arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ixgbevf: fix use-after-free in VEPA multicast source pruning
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel's ixgbevf virtual function network driver, and is rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security. In ixgbevf_clean_rx_irq(), the VEPA multicast source-pruning workaround frees a received socket buffer (skb) but leaves the skb pointer set; on the next loop iteration the driver can call ixgbevf_add_rx_frag() on the freed skb, dereferencing freed memory in NAPI softirq context. An attacker able to deliver specially crafted network traffic that reaches this receive path under the required conditions could cause a kernel crash (denial of service) or, in some cases, arbitrary code execution. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 Extended Lifecycle Support is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that stream. The affected Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernel and kernel-rt streams and the Red Hat In-Vehicle OS kernels are impacted, and fixes are being pursued through the delegated kernel maintenance process. Red Hat rates this issue 7.0 (Important, CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), notably lower than the CVE program's 9.8 Critical rating, because successful exploitation requires an attacker with local privileges and favorable timing conditions on the affected receive path.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm/khugepaged) component. A local user could trigger an edge case where unsaved changes to file data (dirty folios) are improperly discarded. This occurs when a file with previous writes is subjected to a specific sequence of memory advice (madvise) operations for transparent huge pages (THPs), leading to data loss.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because triggering it requires local access and an uncommon, tightly sequenced series of file modifications and memory collapse requests. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, transparent huge page operations and writable file handles are mutually isolated, limiting the likelihood of unintentional data loss. Additionally, the flaw cannot be leveraged for privilege escalation or remote code execution, restricting the potential damage to the loss of unsaved file modifications accessible to the local user.

Successful exploitation requires an unprivileged local user to operate within a namespace capable of depleting the socket table, which can lead to a system crash or potential privilege escalation.

cwe.name: Incorrect Implementation of Authentication Algorithm

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) authentication mechanism within the Linux kernel. The `sctp_auth_chunk_verify()` function incorrectly processes authentication chunks, leading to authentication requirements being silently bypassed. This can occur under specific conditions, such as when memory allocation fails or when an authentication chunk is missing before a COOKIE-ECHO message. An attacker could potentially exploit this to bypass intended security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: sctp: auth: verify auth requirement when auth_chunk is NULL
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw in the Linux kernel Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) authentication handling, rated MODERATE by Red Hat, affects the kernel and kernel-rt components in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 through 10 (including ELS and z-stream update streams) as well as kernel components in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The sctp_auth_chunk_verify() function returns true unconditionally when chunk->auth_chunk is NULL, so SCTP authentication requirements can be silently skipped when skb_clone() fails in the bottom-half receive path or when no AUTH chunk precedes a COOKIE-ECHO chunk. Under those conditions, an attacker able to deliver crafted SCTP traffic to a system that enforces SCTP chunk authentication could have unauthenticated chunks processed as authenticated, compromising the integrity of SCTP associations. Red Hat's MODERATE rating reflects the high attack complexity and specific preconditions required for exploitation, which differs meaningfully from the CRITICAL (CVSS 9.8) severity assigned in the upstream CVE record. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat products through the delegated kernel maintenance process.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) implementation. When processing a Stream Reset Incoming Request (RESET_IN_REQUEST) from a peer, the kernel does not properly validate the stream count. This can lead to an integer overflow when calculating the size for the corresponding outgoing request, resulting in an undersized memory allocation. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability on interfaces supporting large Maximum Transmission Units (MTU) to trigger a kernel bug, causing a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: sctp: validate stream count in sctp_process_strreset_inreq()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires specific and atypical network configurations, specifically network interfaces configured with a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) greater than 65535 bytes, such as IPv6 jumbograms or local loopback. In standard deployment environments, network frames are constrained to standard MTU boundaries where the integer calculation cannot trigger an allocation error. Furthermore, an attacker must have established communication over an active SCTP association to send stream reset requests, limiting exposure primarily to systems providing SCTP services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) implementation. An incorrect array size calculation for the `auth_hmacs` field within the `sctp_cookie` structure could lead to a buffer overflow. During the initialization of an SCTP association, if four HMAC identifiers are configured, the system attempts to copy data beyond the allocated buffer. This results in the corruption of an adjacent memory field (`auth_chunks`) and can subsequently cause an out-of-bounds read when processing HMAC identifiers.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Wi-Fi subsystem (cfg80211). The `cfg80211_is_element_inherited()` function does not properly validate the length of extension elements. A remote attacker, by sending a specially crafted Wi-Fi frame from an Access Point (AP), could trigger a one-octet slab-out-of-bounds read during element parsing. This could lead to information disclosure or potentially other impacts.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: Linux kernel: Wi-Fi subsystem out-of-bounds read via crafted frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because exploitation requires wireless networking hardware and radio proximity to a rogue access point. Most enterprise server deployments do not utilize Wi-Fi interfaces, greatly restricting the attack surface in standard production environments. On affected client or edge devices, an untrusted wireless access point can trigger a single-byte read beyond buffer boundaries during frame parsing, potentially causing a system crash or limited kernel information disclosure rather than arbitrary code execution.

To mitigate this issue, disable the Wi-Fi functionality if it is not required. This can be done by blacklisting the `cfg80211` kernel module.

1. Create a new file `/etc/modprobe.d/disable-wifi.conf` with the following content:

```
blacklist cfg80211
```

```bash
sudo dracut -f -v
```
3. Reboot the system for the changes to take effect.

This mitigation will prevent the `cfg80211` module, and thus Wi-Fi, from loading. This may impact network connectivity if Wi-Fi is the primary or only network interface.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to create arbitrary Git directories outside the intended clone destination. By manipulating the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning, an attacker can redirect repository metadata to an attacker-controlled filesystem path. This could lead to arbitrary directory creation and potentially enable the execution of malicious code through Git hooks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Arbitrary Code Execution via Path Traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has identified a path traversal vulnerability in GitPython versions before 3.1.59. The vulnerability arises because the `--separate-git-dir` option is not included in the `unsafe_git_clone_options` denylist, allowing attackers who control the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning to redirect Git repository metadata to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended clone destination. This can lead to arbitrary directory and file creation bounded only by process permissions. When combined with subsequent Git operations that trigger hook execution on the redirected repository, this vulnerability can escalate to arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that the application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the `separate_git_dir` keyword argument of `Repo.clone_from()` or `Repo.clone()` methods without proper validation, while the `allow_unsafe_options` parameter remains at its default value of False.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Google Brotli decoder. An out-of-bounds write in the block-type switch handling in c/dec/decode.c can be triggered by a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. When an application decompresses untrusted Brotli data, this can lead to memory disclosure, denial of service, or potentially arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: brotli: Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This issue is rated Important. Exploitation requires that the target decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (for example HTTP content negotiated with Content-Encoding: br, or APIs such as Node.js zlib / fetch() that decode Brotli). The vulnerable path is reached with a malformed stream rather than typical well-formed encoder output, and there is no public, reliable remote code execution proof-of-concept. Red Hat Enterprise Linux compiler and runtime hardenings - including Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), Non-eXecutable (NX) memory, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux - increase the difficulty of turning this memory corruption into reliable code execution, though they do not eliminate crashes or all impact. Combined with the Attack Requirements noted by the CNA (CVSS v4 AT:P), Red Hat scores Attack Complexity as High and rates the flaw Important rather than Critical.

---

The Node.js packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux use either system version of brotli or bundled version. Some Node.js versions are marked "Not affected" because they utilize system brotli. For these versions, the Node.js package itself does not require updating. However, customers must still update the system brotli/libbrotli package to address the vulnerability for these Node.js installations.

Following is the overview of Node.js versions use system or bundled version.

- Node.js 22 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:22 module, uses system brotli.
- Node.js 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:24 modules, use bundled brotli.
- Node.js 22 and 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, provided via nodejs22 and nodejs24 use system brotli.

---

The .NET packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux may either use system version of brotli or bundled version. Following is the overview of .NET versions use system or bundled version.

- .NET 8.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet8.0 packages, use bundled brotli.
- .NET 9.0, 10.0, and 11.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet9.0, dotnet10.0, and dotnet11.0 packages, use system brotli.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When saving compressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images into memory buffers rather than direct files, the library incorrectly calculates the required memory allocation. A remote attacker who supplies a crafted image for processing can trigger a heap-based buffer overflow, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) through process crashes. Additionally, uninitialized memory gaps can result in information disclosure by leaking remnants of previously stored data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The attack complexity is high and also for services that do hit this code path (image upload → TIFF re-encode to BytesIO → return/upload), the minimal PoC reliably crashes the worker process. The heap corruption could plausibly be developed into RCE by a skilled attacker who has already compromised the same process enough to leak addresses, but that's a chained-exploit scenario, not a standalone wormable RCE.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When parsing a crafted GIF image, the library fails to discard rejected frame dimensions after encountering an excessively large image exception. If an application catches this exception and continues processing the image, subsequent operations attempt to allocate memory based on the oversized dimensions. A remote attacker can exploit this issue to exhaust system memory, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion from crafted GIF image
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can supply a malicious graphic file that forces extensive memory allocations, leading to daemon termination or denial of service. The flaw requires consuming applications to catch decompression bomb exceptions and reuse the same image object across subsequent frame operations, allowing oversized geometry values to trigger high resource exhaustion. Exposure is largely concentrated in containerized services and image-processing pipelines that handle untrusted animation uploads directly.

A remote attacker who can submit large image transformation operations under memory pressure can trigger improper error handling, leading to a double-free vulnerability (releasing the same memory block twice). Applications that sanitize image bounds or avoid exposing custom affine transform endpoints remain largely unaffected by this crash condition.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to achieve arbitrary code execution or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted lossless JPEG image to an application that downscales images or generates thumbnails. This issue occurs because the JPEG decoder fails to verify actual output dimensions against the allocated memory buffer during scaling, causing full-width image data to be written beyond buffer boundaries. Successful exploitation leads to heap memory corruption, resulting in an application crash or potential code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in ImagingJpegDecode
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The overflow only triggers when the application calls `draft()` or `thumbnail()` before loading the image. Direct `Image.open().load()` or `Image.open().resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Many image processing pipelines use `load()` followed by `resize()`, not `thumbnail()`. The libjpeg-turbo 3.x requirement, specific code path, and dimension threshold make this **not easily exploitable** across the entire Pillow install base.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When processing Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images, the library fails to properly validate buffer boundaries during tile and color decoding routines. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted TIFF file with conflicting metadata tags, causing an out-of-bounds read. Successful exploitation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the application, or result in information disclosure by exposing adjacent heap memory in the output image.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in TIFF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit it to terminate backend worker processes or leak adjacent heap contents without requiring elevated privileges. Red Hat products utilizing Pillow within containerized services, AI model serving, or automation workflows may be exposed if they accept and parse untrusted TIFF files. Because TIFF parsing occurs automatically during standard image opening routines without requiring custom decode flags, services that ingest user-provided media are susceptible to denial of service or memory exposure.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted image file to an application that processes images with the library. This issue occurs because the Image.merge() function fails to properly validate the first input band, allowing mismatched image storage formats to trigger a null pointer dereference. Consequently, processing the malformed image causes the native application process to crash.

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via null pointer dereference in Image.merge()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash service worker processes handling user uploads without requiring privileges or prior interaction. Because parsing an invalid image file triggers an immediate segmentation fault within the native extension, the issue causes service disruption, although it does not compromise data confidentiality or allow arbitrary code execution.

cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) through an infinite loop during PDF page processing. When rewriting pages, the parser fails to detect circular references in the page tree hierarchy. By submitting a specially crafted PDF document to an application that modifies or appends images to it, an attacker can exhaust system CPU resources and make the service unresponsive.

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via infinite loop during PDF page rewriting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote user can supply a crafted document to trigger an infinite processing loop, resulting in complete CPU core exhaustion and denial of service for the target application worker. The issue specifically threatens services or workloads that ingest untrusted PDFs and append or save pages to them. Standard image parsing and reading pipelines that do not modify or append to existing PDF structures remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Paint (MSP) image file to an application that processes image pixels. Due to missing expansion limits during decompression, the run-length encoding (RLE) decoder expands image data into an unbounded memory buffer, resulting in memory exhaustion and application crashes.

Deployments that process only verified internal content or do not expose image analysis to external inputs face substantially lower operational risk.

Successful exploitation can lead to memory corruption or an application crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

Across Red Hat product environments, Pillow operates as an underlying imaging component in automated services and containerized workloads. The vulnerability is only triggered if an application accepts untrusted font files from users and renders text using non-zero stroke widths, leaving services that utilize standard system fonts unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted PDF document to an application performing PDF append operations. Because the PDF parser fails to properly track cyclic or deeply nested object references, processing the malicious document can consume excessive CPU and memory resources or trigger an application crash.

Standard deployments that do not append to external PDF files or that generate new documents from trusted sources are unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When saving or re-encoding a Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) image containing inconsistent color map metadata, the encoder reads beyond an allocated memory buffer. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted image, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or information disclosure of heap memory.

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in TIFF encoder

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can supply crafted image files over network endpoints to cause process termination or heap memory disclosure without requiring privileges. The impact primarily concerns applications and containerized services that ingest untrusted image data and subsequently re-encode or save it using the libtiff-backed encoder while retaining metadata. Environments and workflows that only read, validate, or display images without writing them back out to TIFF format are not affected.

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This flaw can lead to information disclosure when handling compressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images. During incomplete decoding of image data, uninitialized buffer memory is not cleared before being converted into pixel rows. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted TIFF image to an application that decodes and returns or re-encodes the image, allowing them to view stale contents from heap memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Information disclosure via uninitialized buffer in TIFF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit default image parsing workflows to extract sensitive process memory without requiring privileges or triggering application crashes. In Red Hat environments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform, backend services that ingest user-provided images and return rendered thumbnails, previews, or re-encoded files inadvertently disclose previously freed heap data from concurrent or prior operations. The vulnerability requires processing compressed TIFF files where the decoder handles truncated image streams, meaning services that reject this format or never expose generated image outputs are not impacted.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying an untrusted submodule path. Because the library fails to properly validate destination paths before cloning repository data, an attacker can plant a malicious executable script into sensitive directories, such as the Git hooks folder. Subsequent Git operations then trigger the planted script, executing commands in the context of the running application.

In Red Hat environments, such as Ansible Automation Platform, OpenShift AI, and Red Hat Satellite, impact is limited to workloads configured to process repository structures from untrusted or unauthenticated sources.

notes.text:
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes provides the
capabilities to address common challenges that administrators and site
reliability engineers face as they work across a range of public and
private cloud environments. Clusters and applications are all visible and
managed from a single console—with security policy built in.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat Advanced Cluster
Management for Kubernetes, which add new features and enhancements, bug
fixes, and updated container images. See the following
Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this
release, for additional details about this release:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.13/html-single/release_notes/index#acm-release-notes

notes.text: On instances using Auth Proxy header authentication ([auth.proxy]) with identity caching enabled (sync_ttl > 0), two distinct user identities could produce the same cache key. An authenticated low-privileged user able to influence their own forwarded identity attributes could be served a higher-privileged user's cached session and act as that user for the duration of the cache TTL. Default configurations are not affected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: Grafana: Session takeover via Auth Proxy cache key collision
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact because successful exploitation allows an authenticated user to hijack sessions of administrative or privileged accounts, leading to complete compromise of the application. The flaw requires non-default settings where reverse proxy header-based authentication is enabled alongside active identity caching. In standard Red Hat product deployments, header-based proxy authentication is not enabled by default, which substantially limits the attack surface across standard installations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. When extracting plugin archives, Grafana did not safely resolve symbolic links. A remote attacker could craft a malicious plugin archive with symbolic links to escape the plugin installation directory. This allows the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute malicious code with the privileges of the Grafana server process, leading to remote code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: PLUGIN ARCHIVE EXTRACTION ESCAPES THE PLUGIN DIRECTORY, ALLOWING CODE EXECUTION
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Grafana's plugin extraction process is vulnerable to symbolic link traversal, enabling an attacker to write arbitrary files and achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the Grafana server. This critical flaw allows malicious code execution even before plugin signature verification, posing a significant risk in Red Hat deployments where Grafana is used.

remediations.details: While no configuration fully mitigates this issue, exposure can be reduced by limiting plugin installations to vetted and pinned sets of plugins from trusted sources. Additionally, disable the `plugin_admin_enabled` setting in the Grafana configuration if not required, to prevent non-administrator users from installing plugins. This can be done by setting `plugin_admin_enabled = false` in the `[plugins]` section of the `grafana.ini` configuration file. A restart of the Grafana service may be required for changes to take effect, which could temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in grpc-gateway up to v2.28.0. A remote attacker could exploit an incorrect access control vulnerability by sending a specially crafted POST request that includes the X-HTTP-Method-Override header. The application processes this header without restricting allowed methods, allowing the request method to be rewritten to an arbitrary attacker-supplied value before routing. This bypasses method-based access controls enforced by upstream proxies or Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), potentially leading to unauthorized actions or information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2: grpc-gateway: Access control bypass via X-HTTP-Method-Override header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact for Red Hat products because exploitation requires a deployment where upstream reverse proxies or perimeter filters enforce access control solely based on HTTP methods without stripping method-override headers. In typical Red Hat deployments, backend gRPC services enforce their own authentication and authorization controls, limiting an attacker's ability to execute unauthorized actions simply by tunneling rewritten request verbs.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The component failed to properly enforce source-address restrictions for several authentication methods, including password and keyboard-interactive callbacks. In applications that misuse the ServerConfig.PublicKeyCallback callback to make security relevant authorization decisions, an attacker with a valid key could bypass network-based access controls to gain additional privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Authentication bypass due to unenforced source-address restrictions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability severity is Important due to the requirement that an attacker already have a valid private key. A flaw in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh allows remote attackers to bypass source-address restrictions for certain authentication methods. This would allow an attacker to use a valid key for gaining additional privileges outside of the bounds of the network-based access controls.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in kin-openapi, a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. An unauthenticated client can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted query with a large index in a deepObject query parameter. This forces the application to allocate multi-gigabyte memory, leading to an Out-of-Memory (OOM) error or a restart loop, effectively causing a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of Service via uncontrolled resource consumption in deepObject query parameter decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a small request can exhaust memory and terminate an exposed service. Exploitation requires an application to decode attacker-controlled query parameters using kin-openapi’s deepObject handling with an array-containing schema. Schema limits such as maxItems do not prevent the allocation, and HTTP handler panic recovery does not protect against process termination from memory exhaustion.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. The tlsConfigFromURI helper creates tls.Config values for amqps:// URIs without setting MinVersion. When the client is built with a Go toolchain whose default still permits TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1, a network attacker who can influence TLS negotiation may force an obsolete protocol version and weaken protection of AMQP messages and credentials. The issue is fixed in amqp091-go 1.13.0 by requiring TLS 1.2 as the minimum.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Missing Explicit TLS Minimum Version Configuration In URI Parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Red Hat product streams that ship amqp091-go before 1.13.0 are Affected because tlsConfigFromURI does not set an explicit TLS MinVersion when parsing AMQPS URIs. Exploitation requires a man-in-the-middle position on the path to the AMQP broker; Go 1.18 or later client defaults further raise complexity by preferring TLS 1.2 when MinVersion is unset. Streams that already ship amqp091-go 1.13.0 or later contain the explicit fix and are Not affected. The issue is not Critical because it is not remotely exploitable without those high-complexity prerequisites, and it does not provide unauthenticated remote code execution.

notes.text: RabbitMQ amqp091-go versions before 1.13.0 mishandle an oversized AMQP longstr field. A malicious or compromised broker can desynchronize message parsing, causing subsequent bytes to be interpreted as AMQP data and disrupting connection integrity or availability. Fixed in version 1.13.0.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Protocol Desynchronization and Frame Injection via Integer Overflow in readLongstr
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw affects Red Hat products using the vulnerable RabbitMQ amqp091-go client. Exploitation requires a malicious or compromised AMQP broker and may disrupt client connections or cause unintended protocol processing. Red Hat rates this issue Important.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust process memory by sending millions of fragmented HTTP/2 DATA frames. Each fragmented frame is stored as a separate message, consuming disproportionate heap memory. This can lead to a runtime panic or out-of-memory termination, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 DATA Frame Fragmentation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust memory and crash affected applications without exceeding connection flow-control windows. Within Red Hat OpenShift and containerized platforms, gRPC-Go is embedded in various internal control plane agents, monitoring exporters, and management components. Although services handling untrusted remote gRPC traffic remain susceptible to denial of service, exposure in standard cluster deployments is constrained because these interfaces typically operate across isolated internal networks or behind mutual TLS boundaries.

notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: js-yaml: js-yaml: Denial of Service vulnerability in YAML parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in js-yaml, affecting applications that process untrusted YAML input. The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.

If upgrading go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to version 1.17.10 (v1) or 2.9.1 (v2) is not immediately possible, the following steps can reduce exposure:
- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. The lookupProperty own-property check returns Function.prototype.constructor before the prototype-method deny list is applied. When an attacker can render a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault enabled and an accessible function in the template context, arbitrary JavaScript can execute with the application process privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires rendering a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault set to true (off by default) and an accessible function in the template context, allowing bypass of the constructor deny list via Function.prototype. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because those non-default runtime conditions raise attack complexity (AC:H); default Handlebars configurations that keep allowProtoMethodsByDefault disabled are not exploitable for this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

notes.text:
Red Hat multicluster engine for Kubernetes v2.8 general availability release images, which provide security fixes, bug fixes, and updated container images.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE links in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The multicluster engine for Kubernetes provides the foundational components
that are necessary for the centralized management of multiple
Kubernetes-based clusters across data centers, public clouds, and private
clouds.

You can use the engine to create new Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
clusters or to bring existing Kubernetes-based clusters under management by
importing them. After the clusters are managed, you can use the APIs that
are provided by the engine to distribute configuration based on placement
policy.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to.
