notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

This flaw allows a malicious user to randomly cause an uninitialized buffer length variable with a zeroed buffer to be returned in FIPS mode. cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.

Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go `net` package, affecting applications configured to use the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could trigger a double-free memory error by providing a very long CNAME response, leading to a crash of the vulnerable application and impacting service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.

notes.text: crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go standard library's certificate chain building process. Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via long CNAME response in LookupCNAME
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go `net` package, affecting applications configured to use the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could trigger a double-free memory error by providing a very long CNAME response, leading to a crash of the vulnerable application and impacting service availability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. This can be achieved by setting the `GODEBUG` environment variable to `netdns=go`. For example, to run a Go application with this mitigation: `GODEBUG=netdns=go /path/to/your/go/application`. This change may require restarting affected applications or services to take effect. Users should verify that this change does not negatively impact DNS resolution for their specific application environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

notes.text: A flaw was found in go-git, an extensible Git implementation library. Worktree operations, such as checkout, status, and add, resolve symbolic links within the working tree without proper boundary confinement. This allows a remote attacker to craft a malicious repository containing a symlink, which, when cloned and its worktree operations are used, can lead to reading from or writing to arbitrary files outside the intended working directory. This could result in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/go-git/go-git/v5: go-git: Arbitrary file read/write via symbolic link resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: go-git is a pure-Go implementation of Git. During worktree operations (checkout, status, add), go-git resolves symbolic links without confining resolution to the worktree boundary, so a maliciously crafted repository containing a symlink can cause a consuming application to read from or write to files outside the intended working directory when that repository is cloned and its worktree operations are used. Exploitation requires the application to clone an attacker-controlled repository and then perform worktree operations against it; applications that only process trusted repositories are not exposed. Red Hat rates the impact of this flaw as Important.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.

The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/url package in the Go standard library. The package does not enforce a limit on the number of unique query parameters it parses. A Go application using the net/http.Request.ParseForm method will try to process all parameters provided in the request. A specially crafted HTTP request containing a massive number of query parameters will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory, eventually causing the application to crash or become unresponsive, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/url: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be able to send a specially crafted HTTP request to an application parsing URL-encoded forms with net/url, specifically a request containing a large number of unique query parameters. The request will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory and eventually result in a denial of service, with no impact to confidentiality or integrity. Due to this reason, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).

This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.

To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. This can be achieved by setting the `GODEBUG` environment variable to `netdns=go`. For example, to run a Go application with this mitigation: `GODEBUG=netdns=go /path/to/your/go/application`. This change may require restarting affected applications or services to take effect. Users should verify that this change does not negatively impact DNS resolution for their specific application environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in etcd, a distributed key-value store. A remote attacker can exploit this by opening numerous TCP connections to an etcd TLS listener without completing the TLS handshake. This action causes the `tlsListener.acceptLoop` to spawn an unbounded number of goroutines, which consume excessive memory. This resource exhaustion leads to a Denial of Service (DoS) for the etcd cluster and, consequently, for the Kubernetes control plane it supports.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces provides a cloud developer workspace server and a  browser-based IDE built for teams and organizations. Dev Spaces runs in  OpenShift and is well-suited for container-based development. 
The 3.31 release is based on Eclipse Che 7.123.x and uses the DevWorkspace engine  to provide support for workspaces based on devfile v2.1 and v2.2. 
Users still using the v1 standard should migrate as soon as possible. 
https://devfile.io/docs/2.2.0/migrating-to-devfile-v2 
Dev Spaces supports OpenShift EUS releases v4.16 and higher. Users are  expected to update to supported OpenShift releases in order to continue to get Dev  Spaces updates. 
https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift#crw

notes.text: A flaw was found in zod. A remote attacker can trigger a denial of service (DoS) by submitting an excessively large array of invalid items to an application that validates input schemas without length constraints. Because the validation process accumulates error records for each failing element without a cap or early exit, the application consumes excessive memory and crashes due to an out-of-memory condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: zod: zod: Denial of service via unbounded array validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated with an Important severity because remote attackers can induce complete service unavailability through process termination without requiring privileged access. Within Red Hat environments, the affected library is embedded into multiple management consoles and microservices that process structured user data. The operational impact depends on whether exposed network endpoints evaluate untrusted collections without preliminary restrictions on payload sizes or element counts.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Axios, a promise-based HTTP client. This vulnerability occurs because Axios does not correctly handle hostname normalization when evaluating NO_PROXY rules. An attacker can exploit this by crafting requests to loopback addresses (e.g., localhost. or [::1]) which bypass the NO_PROXY configuration and are routed through the configured proxy. This can lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities, enabling attackers to access sensitive internal or loopback services that should otherwise be protected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: axios: Axios: Server-Side Request Forgery and proxy bypass due to improper hostname normalization
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has limited impact due to combination of non-default conditions to exploit: the attacker must be able to control or influence URLs passed to axios in a server-side context, the application must have both `HTTP_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` configured, and the proxy itself must be positioned to act on the misdirected traffic or have been compromised by the attacker to intercept the rerouted traffic.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pip, the package installer for Python. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by tricking a victim into installing a malicious Python wheel. This wheel contains specially crafted entry-point names that use directory traversal or absolute paths. This allows pip to write generated script wrappers outside the intended installation directory, leading to arbitrary file overwrite. This can severely impact system integrity and availability, and in certain scenarios, may lead to arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python-pip: Path traversal via malicious entry point name in pip wheel installation allows arbitrary file overwrite
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important flaw in pip's wheel installation process allows for arbitrary file overwrite due to path traversal. An attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to install a specially crafted malicious Python wheel. While file overwrites are limited to the installing user's permissions, using `pip install` with elevated privileges in Red Hat environments significantly increases the potential impact, potentially leading to system integrity compromise or arbitrary code execution.

It is strongly advised against using `pip install` with elevated privileges, such as `sudo`, when installing wheels. notes.text: A flaw was found in the pacote component. A remote attacker can exploit this denial of service (DoS) vulnerability by providing a specially crafted input to the `addGitSha` function. This malicious input triggers excessive CPU consumption due to regex replacement and string manipulation, which can lead to the process stalling or crashing.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pacote: Pacote: Denial of Service via crafted spec.rawSpec value in addGitSha function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the pacote npm package. Pacote retrieves package metadata and archives from npm registries, Git repositories, and other sources. In affected versions, the addGitSha function strips Git committish information from a package specification using a regular expression that is vulnerable to inefficient backtracking. An attacker who can supply a crafted spec.rawSpec value can cause the Node.js process that calls pacote to consume excessive CPU and become unresponsive, resulting in denial of service.

Red Hat products that include pacote versions from 11.2.7 up to (but not including) 21.5.1 may be affected when Node.js workloads process package specifications through pacote or through npm operations that depend on pacote. The impact is limited to the Node.js process performing that work; host operating systems are not directly affected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Bouncy Castle for Java. The BKS/UBER keystore component allocates memory based on untrusted length values before performing an integrity check. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted keystore, leading to excessive memory allocation and a denial of service (DoS) condition.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in Bouncy Castle for Java allows a remote attacker to trigger excessive memory allocation by providing a specially crafted BKS/UBER keystore. This can lead to a denial of service in applications that process untrusted keystores, such as those found in Red Hat Enterprise Application Platform and Red Hat JBoss Fuse. The impact is limited to denial of service and requires user interaction to process the malicious input.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. This vulnerability allows for cross-user information disclosure when malformed Cache-Control private directives cause private response bodies and headers, such as Set-Cookie data, to be stored in a shared cache and subsequently exposed to other users. Additionally, a specially crafted Cache-Control header can trigger an unhandled error in the cache parser, leading to a process termination and a Denial of Service (DoS). Both issues affect applications using the cache interceptor in shared mode.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Bouncy Castle for Java, including its LTS and FIPS variants. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to trigger an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) error by providing specially crafted input during a definite-length read operation. This unbounded memory allocation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS), making the affected system or application unavailable.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.bouncycastle/bcprov-jdk15on: org.bouncycastle/bcprov-jdk18on: org.bouncycastle/bc-fips: org.bouncycastle/bctls-fips: Bouncy Castle for Java: Denial of Service due to unbounded memory allocation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Bouncy Castle for Java is bundled as a cryptographic provider across numerous Red Hat products. An unbounded up-front memory allocation on a definite-length read lets a remote attacker trigger an Out-Of-Memory condition with crafted input, resulting in a denial of service. This is broadly reachable wherever Bouncy Castle parses untrusted encoded data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Eclipse Vert.x Web Client. The WebClientSession component does not properly validate the Domain attribute of a Set-Cookie response header against the originating server's domain. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject a cookie scoped to an arbitrary third-party domain. When the victim application subsequently sends a request to the targeted domain, the injected cookie is presented, potentially leading to information disclosure and unauthorized access to sensitive data through the attacker's account on that service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.vertx/vertx-web: Eclipse Vert.x Web Client: Information disclosure via improper cookie domain validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important information disclosure flaw in Eclipse Vert.x Web Client's `WebClientSession` component. The vulnerability arises from insufficient validation of the `Domain` attribute in `Set-Cookie` response headers, allowing a remote attacker to inject cookies scoped to arbitrary third-party domains. This could lead to sensitive data exposure and unauthorized access if a victim application subsequently sends requests to the targeted domain, presenting the attacker-controlled cookie. The impact is significant as it bypasses expected cross-domain security boundaries.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the XsltView component of Spring MVC applications. This
vulnerability could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to perform
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), enabling them to make unauthorized
requests from the server, and potentially achieve Remote Code Execution
(RCE), allowing them to execute arbitrary code on the affected system. This
occurs when an application uses a broad URL mapping that results in view
rendering without explicitly specifying the view name, allowing an attacker
to control which stylesheet is loaded.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.springframework/spring-webmvc: Spring Framework: Remote Code Execution via improper path limitation in XsltView
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Critical, a higher severity than the
Medium rating assigned by the Spring project. This vulnerability requires a
remote, unauthenticated attacker with no user interaction to trigger
Server-Side Request Forgery and, depending on the XSLT processor's
configuration, Remote Code Execution — conditions that meet Red Hat's
definition of Critical impact regardless of the upstream CVSS vector.

Exploitation requires a Spring MVC application to use XsltView in
combination with a broad ("/**") URL mapping that renders a view without
explicitly specifying the view name. This is not the default configuration
for Spring MVC applications; applications that explicitly specify view
names, or do not use XsltView, are not exposed.

Where this precondition is met, no additional privileges, authentication,
or user interaction are required, and full compromise of the affected
system is possible via Remote Code Execution. Red Hat is not aware of any
built-in safeguard in affected Spring Framework versions that reduces this
impact once the vulnerable configuration pattern is present.

Independent parties, including CISA-ADP, have also assessed this
vulnerability as Critical, consistent with Red Hat's rating.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata  relevant to your system have been applied. 
For details on how to apply this update, refer to: 
https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

There is no upstream-provided workaround; the Spring project's guidance is
to upgrade to a fixed version. However, applications can avoid this
vulnerability without upgrading by not using XsltView together with a
broad/catch-all URL mapping that omits an explicit view name — explicitly
specifying the view name for any controller or handler that renders a view
prevents an attacker from controlling which XSLT stylesheet is loaded.

For Red Hat Fuse 7, which is in Extended Life Support Phase
2 and will not receive a fix for this issue, this configuration-based
workaround is the only available mitigation.

vulnerabilities.title: org.springframework/spring-webmvc: Spring Framework: Remote Code Execution via improper path limitation in XsltView

notes.text: A flaw was found in Spring Framework. Applications that process user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack. notes.text: Spring Framework: org.springframework/spring-expression: Spring Framework: Denial of Service via unbounded exponentiation in SpEL expressions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A vulnerability was found in Spring Framework's Spring Expression Language (SpEL) engine. When evaluating untrusted SpEL expressions containing the power operator (^) with a BigDecimal or BigInteger operand and an excessively large exponent, the expression parser performs unbounded mathematical calculations. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can supply crafted SpEL queries to consume excessive CPU and memory resources, causing application thread exhaustion and resulting in a denial of service (DoS). Default container resource limits (cgroup memory and CPU quotas) constrain host-level impact, though application process unresponsiveness or crashes remain unavoidable.

(headers(...)) in WebFlux functional endpoint configurations to enforce
security-relevant access control, since this bypass allows such guards to

notes.text: A flaw was found in Bouncy Castle for Java. A remote attacker could exploit this by presenting a stapled Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) response that is not properly bound to the certificate being checked. This vulnerability allows for a certificate validation bypass, potentially leading to applications accepting invalid or revoked certificates. This could enable man-in-the-middle attacks or unauthorized access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.bouncycastle/bcpkix-jdk15on: org.bouncycastle/bcprov-jdk15on: Bouncy Castle for Java: Certificate validation bypass via stapled OCSP response
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This vulnerability in Bouncy Castle for Java allows a remote attacker to bypass certificate validation. By presenting a stapled OCSP response not properly bound to the certificate being checked, an attacker could cause applications to accept invalid or revoked certificates. This could facilitate man-in-the-middle attacks or unauthorized access in Red Hat products that rely on Bouncy Castle for certificate path validation.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

Where Bouncy Castle performs PKIX revocation checking with stapled OCSP, pin expected peer certificate or public-key fingerprints ([CME-404](https://cmetaxonomy.org/entries/CME-404.html)) so a stapled OCSP response for a different serial cannot substitute trust. Restrict TLS clients to trusted networks and peers ([CME-202](https://cmetaxonomy.org/entries/CME-202.html), [CME-203](https://cmetaxonomy.org/entries/CME-203.html)) to reduce man-in-the-middle opportunity against revoked certificates. If stapled OCSP is not required, avoid PKIXRevocationChecker.setOcspResponses() and use CRL or online OCSP fetch paths that enforce CertID binding. Upgrade to Bouncy Castle 1.85 or later (BC-LTS 2.73.12, or bc-fips 2.0.2 / 2.1.3) when available.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Spring Framework. Applications utilizing Spring's data binding infrastructure to apply user-supplied property paths onto a target object are susceptible to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack. notes.text: org.springframework:spring-beans: Spring Framework: Denial of Service via unbounded list growth in data binding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in Spring Framework's property data binding infrastructure within the `spring-beans` module (`AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor`). When processing user-supplied property paths against target objects exposing self-populating List properties, property path navigation invokes `list.get(index)` without validating array bounds after the `autoGrowCollectionLimit` check. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply request parameters with arbitrarily large array indices to force unbounded element allocation. This leads to heap memory exhaustion, application thread unresponsiveness, and process termination, resulting in a denial of service (DoS). Default container resource limits constrain host-level impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Micrometer's StatsD and Logging meter registries. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject line terminators into metric data, such as names or tag values, due to insufficient sanitization of untrusted input. Exploitation can lead to the spoofing of arbitrary metrics, including critical system or business metrics, and the injection of false log entries, potentially impacting monitoring and auditing systems.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.micrometer/micrometer-registry-statsd: io.micrometer/micrometer-core: Micrometer: Line-protocol and log injection via unsanitized input allows metric and log spoofing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A moderate severity flaw was found in Micrometer's StatsD and Logging meter registries (io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-statsd and io.micrometer:micrometer-core), which are shipped in a number of Red Hat middleware, integration, and application-platform products. These libraries do not sanitize newline characters (\n, \r) by default. When an application instruments meters using user-controlled, unvalidated input for metric names, tag keys, or tag values, a remote attacker can inject line terminators to break out of the current metric or log line. With the Datadog or Etsy flavor of the StatsD registry, whose protocol is newline-delimited, this enables line-protocol injection and cross-metric spoofing; with LoggingMeterRegistry, which prints metric output line-by-line to log files, this enables metric spoofing via downstream log-metrics scrapers or parsers as well as general log spoofing. A successful attacker can spoof arbitrary metrics, including critical system or business metrics, and inject false log entries, impacting the integrity of monitoring and auditing systems; the confidentiality and availability of the application itself are not directly affected. Exploitation requires the specific registry configuration together with unsafe instrumentation that passes untrusted input to meters, so attack complexity is high, and Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate (CVSS 3.1: 5.9, AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N), consistent with the upstream MEDIUM rating.

Multiple Red Hat products that ship the affected components, including Red Hat build of Quarkus, JBoss EAP XP, Red Hat Build of Keycloak, JBoss Data Grid, Red Hat AMQ, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and Red Hat build of Apache Camel, are recorded as affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible engineering teams; several affected product streams are out of active support scope. Red Hat Satellite is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the shipped candlepin component.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Spring MVC functional web framework. This vulnerability allows for stream corruption when applications use Server-Sent Events (SSE), a technology for pushing real-time updates from a server to a client. This could lead to unreliable data delivery and impact the integrity of information presented to users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.springframework/spring-webmvc: Spring MVC: Stream corruption via Server-Sent Events (SSE)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Spring Framework functional web framework's Server-Sent Events (SSE) implementation. When plain-text data that an attacker controls is sent through an SSE ServerResponse and contains a bare carriage return (\r), the text can break out of its data field and be interpreted by the browser as new SSE fields. This vulnerability affects applications using RouterFunction and ServerResponse.sse() to send streaming plain-text data. Applications using JSON-serialized events via HttpMessageConverter or annotated controllers with SseEmitter are not affected, as these implementations already escape carriage returns.

Red Hat ships vulnerable versions of Spring Framework in JBoss Fuse 7 (Extended Lifecycle Support), Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces, Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Quarkus (Hawtio), and Subscription Services components.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Micrometer Tracing's Brave bridge when using W3C baggage propagation. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending specially crafted requests with excessively large baggage headers. This can lead to unbounded memory allocation, causing high CPU usage, increased garbage collection, and potentially crashing the application, resulting in a denial of service. notes.text: io.micrometer/micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave: Micrometer Tracing Brave Bridge: Denial of Service via W3C Baggage Propagation

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in Micrometer Tracing's Brave bridge when using W3C baggage propagation. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send HTTP requests with excessively large `baggage` headers containing many key-value pairs, triggering unbounded memory allocation and garbage collection pressure. This can lead to high CPU usage and application crashes via OutOfMemoryError, resulting in a denial of service. This vulnerability affects applications using Spring Boot 3.x or later where W3C and baggage propagation are enabled by default, and where the application processes requests from untrusted sources. The impact depends on whether network components adequately limit HTTP header sizes.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Netty (io.netty:netty-handler). When using the SslProvider.OPENSSL client path with a plain X509TrustManager and without Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping (Java 25+), TLS hostname verification is disabled. This misconfiguration allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to present a fraudulent certificate for a different hostname, which is then accepted without proper validation. This could lead to sensitive information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.netty/netty-handler: Netty: TLS hostname verification bypass via OpenSSL client path misconfiguration
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products ship io.netty:netty-handler as a transitive dependency across multiple middleware and platform products. While the CVSS score reflects the severity of a successful exploit — full confidentiality compromise of TLS-protected traffic without authentication — the vulnerable code path requires three conditions simultaneously: explicit OpenSSL provider configuration, a plain X509TrustManager, and a Java 25+ runtime. Most Red Hat product deployments use the default JDK SSL provider and currently run on Java 21 LTS, making the vulnerable configuration uncommon in practice.

This vulnerability only affects applications that explicitly configure Netty to use the OpenSSL TLS provider (SslProvider.OPENSSL). 

The following mitigations can reduce exposure without applying a patch:

1) Use the default JDK SSL provider — Do not configure SslProvider.OPENSSL in your Netty SslContext setup. The default JDK SSL provider (SslProvider.JDK) is not affected by this vulnerability. Most applications use the JDK default unless explicitly overridden.

2) Use X509ExtendedTrustManager — If the OpenSSL provider is required, ensure the configured trust manager extends X509ExtendedTrustManager rather than the plain X509TrustManager interface. The extended variant performs hostname verification independently of the Netty wrapping logic.

3) Run on Java 24 or earlier — The vulnerable code path only triggers on Java 25+ where sun.misc.Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping is unavailable. Running on earlier Java versions (e.g., Java 21 LTS) means the wrapping works correctly and hostname verification stays enabled.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Traefik. Traefik's HTTP reverse proxy can improperly handle HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 CONNECT requests forwarded to an HTTP/1.1 upstream. If the upstream sends a keep-alive non-2xx response and does not fully drain the body, the desynchronized backend socket is returned to a shared pool. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by making a different client read their smuggled response, which can lead to information disclosure, potentially exposing authenticated or private content from other requests. The ForwardAuth middleware can also be affected, further exposing the authentication client pool to desynchronization.

notes.text: A desynchronization flaw in Traefik's HTTP reverse proxy allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to perform HTTP request smuggling. When forwarding HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 CONNECT requests to an HTTP/1.1 upstream that responds with a keep-alive non-2xx status without draining the request body, Traefik re-adds the tainted connection to its shared transport pool. Subsequent requests from other clients reused on this socket read the attacker's smuggled response, leading to cross-tenant data leakage or exposed authentication credentials, bypassing non-root container boundaries.

notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. The `qs.stringify` function, responsible for serializing objects, does not properly validate the `isBuffer` property of an object's constructor before attempting to invoke it. An unauthenticated attacker can provide specially crafted input that, when processed and then serialized by `qs.stringify`, triggers a `TypeError`. notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by sending a specially crafted query string to an application using `qs.parse` with specific non-default settings (`comma: true` and `throwOnLimitExceeded: true`). This bypasses a configured array limit, causing the parser to allocate an excessively large array. This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by consuming too much memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the qs npm package. When an application calls qs.parse() with both comma:true and throwOnLimitExceeded:true enabled (both non-default options), a comma-separated value under a bracket-push key (for example, a[]=1,2,3,4) can bypass the configured arrayLimit and allocate an oversized array, causing denial of service in that application process. This is an incomplete fix for a related issue addressed in qs 6.14.2 (CVE-2026-2391). Red Hat products that bundle qs in the affected version range may be impacted if they parse untrusted query strings or urlencoded request bodies with both options enabled. The availability impact is limited to the application process using qs; host operating systems are not at risk of availability degradation due to this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata  relevant to your system have been applied. 
For details on how to apply this update, refer to: 
https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Applications that do not use BalancedPool, or that use it without a custom function-valued connect/tls option, are not affected and require no action. notes.text: A flaw was found in Colord, a tool for color manipulations. A remote attacker can supply a specially crafted, oversized color string to the affected component. This can cause the processing thread to block, leading to a denial of service (DoS) for the application using Colord.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: colord: omgovich/colord: Colord: Denial of Service via oversized malformed color strings
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) flaw was found in the colord npm package. The synchronous CSS color string matchers in colord use ambiguous regular expressions that exhibit quadratic backtracking when processing malformed input. An attacker who can supply unbounded color strings to the library's parsing functions (such as colord(), getFormat(), isEqual(), mix(), or contrast()) may temporarily block the processing thread.
However, exploitation requires multi-kilobyte payloads to cause a noticeable stall (64 KB for a ~4 second delay), and the growth is polynomial (quadratic), not exponential.
Note: The RHEL RPM packages named "colord" (hughsie/colord) are a completely different C-based color management daemon and are not affected by this vulnerability. Only the npm package "colord" (omgovich/colord) is affected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.4.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When the cache or deduplicate interceptor is directly composed onto a Client or Pool, the destination origin is omitted from cache and request-deduplication keys. This allows a remote attacker to perform cross-origin cache poisoning, leading to information disclosure and potentially a full authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit this by having a trusted origin accept a malicious token, without contacting the legitimate trusted origin.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Authentication bypass via cross-origin cache poisoning due to missing origin isolation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in Traefik, an open-source HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer. Its entrypoint defenses, designed to sanitize header names, failed to inspect request trailers. This allowed an unauthenticated client to submit malicious header names within HTTP/1.1 chunked or HTTP/2 trailers. Consequently, these unsanitized trailer values could reach backend systems, bypassing security controls and potentially leading to identity spoofing or manipulation of routing data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Traefik's request sanitization mechanism. When buffering or retry middleware processes the payload before proxying, these trailer values pass through to backend applications that merge trailers into header namespaces. Under standard Red Hat container execution controls, this allows attackers to bypass configured proxy header deletions, leading to HTTP request smuggling, header spoofing, or unauthorized routing context manipulation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. The generated activation scripts for shells such as bash, zsh, and fish apply improper quoting to environment and library path variables. An attacker can exploit this by providing a crafted virtual environment path containing shell metacharacters. When an unsuspecting user sources the activation script, the embedded metacharacters are executed as shell commands, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of that user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via crafted paths in activation scripts
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled as a dependency in a number of Red Hat products, including Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux container images, Red Hat Hardened Images, and other Red Hat-delivered components. The generated activate (bash and zsh) and activate.fish scripts place path values that were already escaped by shlex.quote inside an additional quoted context. The surplus quotes can terminate the data-only quoted run, leaving shell metacharacters within a crafted value to be parsed as shell commands: in the bash and zsh scripts a crafted virtual environment path is interpolated when a relocated environment's recorded directory is absent, and in the fish script crafted Tcl or Tk library paths are interpolated into __TCL_LIBRARY__ or __TK_LIBRARY__. When a user sources such an activation script, an attacker who controls the crafted path can execute arbitrary code with the privileges of that user. The flaw was rated Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream severity; exploitation requires local control of the affected path values and user interaction to source the activation script. Red Hat product relationships for this flaw are DELEGATED: the impact described above applies where vulnerable virtualenv versions are bundled, fixes are being pursued through the responsible product components, and components where virtualenv is not present in the shipped artifact are being marked not affected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. When fetching seed packages such as pip or setuptools during environment creation or updates, virtualenv does not verify the integrity of downloaded files against authoritative cryptographic checksums. A network attacker or compromised mirror could substitute malicious packages under expected filenames. If virtualenv caches and installs these tampered packages into subsequent environments, an attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via unverified downloaded seed wheels
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped in Red Hat products and offerings including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Red Hat AI offerings, and other Red Hat cloud services. When virtualenv fetches pip or setuptools seed wheels over the network, through its periodic-update mechanism or the --download option, it does not verify the downloaded files against an authoritative cryptographic checksum. A network attacker able to intercept TLS traffic, or a compromised or stale package index or mirror, could substitute a malicious wheel under the expected distribution, version, and filename. virtualenv would then cache the tampered wheel and seed it into subsequently created virtual environments, which can result in arbitrary code execution. Red Hat products that bundle virtualenv are affected where this download path can be exercised, and fixes are being pursued through the respective product release streams; a small number of bundled components were assessed as not affected because the vulnerable component is not present in them. While the upstream project's security advisory rates this issue as low severity, Red Hat rates it as Important based on the potential for arbitrary code execution in environments created from tampered seed packages.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in claude-code. An attacker with write access to a shared workspace can achieve arbitrary file modification and privilege escalation by exploiting a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition. By replacing a project file with a symbolic link between the permission check and the write operation, an attacker can bypass workspace restrictions and overwrite sensitive files outside the project sandbox.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: claude-code: claude-code: Arbitrary file write via TOCTOU race condition
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in Claude Code (claude-code), which is bundled in the Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces plugin registry container image (devspaces/pluginregistry-rhel9) in the 3.28, 3.29, and 3.30 streams. Claude Code validated that a target file path resided within the project working directory at permission-check time, but re-resolved the path at write time without repeating that validation. An attacker with write access to a shared workspace could exploit this time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition by atomically replacing a project file with a symbolic link between the permission check and the write operation, causing Claude Code to follow the symlink and write to an arbitrary file outside the project sandbox. Exploitation requires winning a race against the write operation, but could allow a lower-privileged attacker to redirect benign edits to sensitive files (such as shell configuration) in a higher-privileged session, resulting in arbitrary file modification and privilege escalation. Red Hat rates this flaw as moderate impact (CVSS 7.0, AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) because exploitation requires local access with write access to the shared workspace and successfully winning a race; the upstream advisory rates it High (CVSS 7.7) using a CVSS v4 vector that assumes a network attack vector and no privileges. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces streams with the resolution delegated to the responsible component team.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.
